5139.statement: There is one interpretation of a text and it is your job as a student of English to find the correct interpretation.
5139.correction: Texts rarely have one interpretation, and part of your job as a student of English is to consider the range and then select which one you think is the strongest, whilst still allowing for the idea that some might disagree with you.

11165.belief: If you are writing in third person, then you can't know the internal feelings of characters because you are not inside their head.
11165.statement: If you are writing in third person, then you can't know the internal feelings of characters because you are not inside their head.
11165.correction: Writers that use a third person narrative voice can still explore and present the internal thoughts and feelings of one or more of their characters. You can develop their psychology without having to use the pronoun 'I'.

9366.belief: Skimming and scanning means you just aren't reading a text properly.
9366.statement: Skimming and scanning means you just aren't reading a text properly.
9366.correction: Reading is a skill and, often it is good not to dive into its most difficult skill - analysis - immediately. Instead, giving yourself some time with the text, its title and overall ideas can allow for a deeper understanding in the long run.

5651.belief: Poems are carefully crafted and use methods, but nonfiction letters won't have a structure or include methods.
5651.statement: Poems are carefully crafted and use methods, but nonfiction letters won't have a structure or include methods.
5651.correction: Almost all writing follows some sort of structure even, for example, a shopping list. Methods are tools writers use to convey their messages. Every single word, technically, is a method.

5398.belief: People don't use literary methods in nonfiction writing.
5398.statement: People don't use literary methods in nonfiction writing.
5398.correction: Whenever you write any thing - even a shopping list - you are employing methods. Every word is a choice, thus every choice can be evaluated. In nonfiction writing (even nonfiction writing by people who aren't writers) methods will be used for effect.

11059.belief: Word choice is more important than rhythm.
11059.statement: Word choice is more important than rhythm.
11059.correction: Word choice and powerful literary methods (for example metaphor) are hard things to craft and deserve time and attention. But so too does your sentence construction. Consider if you heard one of your favourite songs but there was no rhythm to it.

10188.correction: A memoir is an account of something based on a person's memories. They are examples of nonfiction.

852.belief: You can't use words, phrases or methods from other people's writing in your own writing.
852.statement: You can't use words, phrases or methods from other people's writing in your own writing.
852.correction: Plagiarism is when you use someone's work or ideas without their consent. This is not allowed. However, you can use texts that inspire and excite you to inform your own writing. This might be a piece of powerful vocabulary or a powerful method.

11125.belief: Working out the tone, audience and purpose is an unnecessary step in planning. These things are always really obvious.
11125.statement: Working out the tone, audience and purpose is an unnecessary step in planning. These things are always really obvious.
11125.correction: The foundations of convincing writing comes in the planning stage. This includes thinking carefully about tone, audience and purpose. Having a deep, rather than superficial, understanding of each will allow for a compelling piece of writing.

3651.belief: It is important to focus on the creation of complex methods like metaphor or anaphora. Verbs don't matter.
3651.statement: It is important to focus on the creation of complex methods like metaphor or anaphora. Verbs don't matter.
3651.correction: Every sentence should contain a verb. As such, choosing them requires careful thought, and can dramatically impact the tone and pace of your writing.

4561.belief: Only men from England fought for Britain.
4561.statement: That only men from England fought for Britain.
4561.correction: Men from all over the British Empire fought for Britain.

5660.belief: A poet had to experience actual fighting to write war poetry.
5660.statement: That a poet had to experience actual fighting to write war poetry.
5660.correction: Though part of the Royal Navy Volunteer Reserve, Brooke saw no military action.

256.belief: Analysing word choice is exclusively part of language analysis.
256.statement: That analysing word choice is exclusively part of language analysis.
256.correction: Analysing where certain words appear in a poem is an effective structural choice.

320.belief: An answer should include all of the interesting details about a text.
320.statement: That an answer should include all of the interesting details about a text.
320.correction: An answer should only include details that are relevant to the question.

10918.belief: All war poetry is designed to dissuade people from fighting.
10918.statement: That all war poetry is designed to dissuade people from fighting.
10918.correction: Pro-war poetry is designed to encourage people to volunteer to fight.

4835.belief: Natural imagery is only designed to help paint a picture to the reader.
4835.statement: That natural imagery is only designed to help paint a picture to the reader.
4835.correction: Natural imagery can also be used to suggest a concept is natural or make a comment about the relationship between humans and nature.

9181.belief: You should always select quotes with the most linguistic features to talk about.
9181.statement: That you should always select quotes with the most linguistic features to talk about.
9181.correction: You should select the quote that best matches the point of the sentence.

9404.belief: Only soldiers from England fought for Britain in WW1.
9404.statement: That only soldiers from England fought for Britain in WW1.
9404.correction: Soldiers from all over the British Empire fought for Britain.

823.belief: You cannot analyse words in structural analysis.
823.statement: That you cannot analyse words in structural analysis.
823.correction: Analysis of where certain words appear in a poem is a valuable structural analysis.

1835.belief: Comparative essays should only focus on the differences between poems.
1835.statement: That comparative essays should only focus on the differences between poems.
1835.correction: The most successful comparative essays focus on both the similarities and the differences between the poems.

1834.belief: A comparative essay should deal with each poem separately in the body of the essay.
1834.statement: A comparative essay should deal with each poem separately in the body of the essay.
1834.correction: While one method of comparison might be to deal with each poem separately, you might also consider comparing the poems throughout the essay and instead splitting up the essay thematically or by methods.

9368.belief: Slam poetry doesn't have any rules or conventions, so anything goes. It's just speaking to an audience.
9368.statement: Slam poetry doesn't have any rules or conventions, so anything goes. It's just speaking to an audience.
9368.correction: While slam poetry encourages creativity and self-expression, it does follow certain conventions, like using sound techniques, imagery and themes. These conventions help poets effectively communicate their messages and engage the audience.

109.belief: Adding "bang" or "crash" to the end of a line or stanza is an effective way to use onomatopoeia.
109.statement: Adding "bang" or "crash" to the end of a line or stanza is an effective way to use onomatopoeia.
109.correction: Although onomatopoeia might seem like an easy device to use, it still needs careful consderation and crafting to be used effectively and creatively.

9369.belief: Slam poetry always has to be serious and about personal or social issues.
9369.statement: Slam poetry always has to be serious and about personal or social issues.
9369.correction: While slam poetry often tackles serious personal and social issues, it can also be playful, humorous or lighthearted. Slam poetry is about expressing yourself in an engaging and authentic way. You can write about anything that matters to you.

6756.statement: Pupils get too nervous to perfom and find public speaking really daunting so they can't do it.
6756.correction: Even the most confident speakers feel nervous! It is completely natural to feel nervous when public speaking. Practising and using specfic strategies will mean they will gradually begin to understand how to work with them.

5389.belief: Only people born in Britain were part of the British Army that fought in WWII.
5389.statement: That only people born in Britain were part of the British Army that fought in WWII.
5389.correction: The British Army contained a huge number of soldiers from different countries. For example, over two and a half million men from the Indian subcontinent volunteered for service, producing the largest volunteer army in history.

88.belief: Adaptations just copy the story from the book. The writer doesn’t have to change much or make many decisions.
88.statement: Adaptations just copy the story from the book. The writer doesn’t have to change much or make many decisions.
88.correction: Adaptations need big changes to work on stage! Edmundson tested scenes in workshops, adjusted them in rehearsals, and watched audience reactions in previews to make sure the story was clear and powerful in performance.

2589.correction: Explore the conventions of a play. What would Edmundson have to have added to re-imagine the novel?

8863.belief: All relevant information comes only from the dialogue in plays.
8863.statement: All relevant information comes only from the dialogue in plays.
8863.correction: What is the role of stage directions? Explore how they are crafted to further characterisation. What extra information do they give us?

4587.belief: Michael and Hortnese have the same upbringing.
4587.statement: Michael and Hortnese have the same upbringing.
4587.correction: As well as exploring the different ways their lives are described, think back to how Mr. Philip reacts to Hortense climbing the tree. Why does he find it so problematic? This reveals a stark difference between Michael and Hortense.

3532.belief: Hortense is only motivated by heartbreak.
3532.statement: That Hortense is only motivated by heartbreak.
3532.correction: How does Hortense view herself, even from a young age? She does at times view herself as superior. Furthermore, she has lived in the house for a long time and has perhaps internalised the moral and religious standards that Mr. Philip holds.

11141.belief: All writers use only original ideas and if they don't they are bad writers.
11141.statement: That all writers use only original ideas and if they don't they are bad writers.
11141.correction: Explore the idea of a literary trope and how writer's use these to elicit specific responses from readers. How do recognisable conventions work to appeal to us as readers?

5365.belief: The Pathé news clips are just old videos used as a backdrop and don’t add meaning to the play.
5365.statement: The Pathé news clips are just old videos used as a backdrop and don’t add meaning to the play.
5365.correction: The Pathé clips set the historical context and show a biased view of the British Empire. They contrast with the characters’ real experiences, deepening our understanding of the story’s themes.

8704.belief: Queenie and Bernard's relationship is only a marriage of convenience.
8704.statement: That Queenie and Bernard's relationship is only a marriage of convenience.
8704.correction: How do Queenie and Bernard interact with each other? Can you find any clues where love or affection might be present?

3871.belief: There isn’t any humour in plays like 'Small Island' because the subject matter is too serious.
3871.statement: There isn’t any humour in plays like 'Small Island' because the subject matter is too serious.
3871.correction: Humour is used in 'Small Island' to make the characters more relatable and to provide moments of relief during tense scenes. It helps the audience connect with the story while still exploring serious issues.

3905.belief: The Jamaican characters all have a cynical view of Britain and the British empire.
3905.statement: The Jamaican characters all have a cynical view of Britain and the British empire.
3905.correction: The reality is more nuanced. Whilst characters like Elwood are openly critical, some characters (like Gilbert) are more positive, buying into wartime narratives of fighting for their 'mother country'.

9174.belief: Segregation only happened in the United States.
9174.statement: That segregation only happened in the United States.
9174.correction: This in the most part is true and Britain certainly didn't have any segregation laws. However, as we see in the play, some individuals and institutions still upheld these ideas of segregation.

584.belief: Because Gilbert jokes and is confident, it means he isn’t really affected by racism or hardship.
584.statement: Because Gilbert jokes and is confident, it means he isn’t really affected by racism or hardship.
584.correction: Gilbert uses humour to hide pain. Arguably, his confidence masks his struggle, making his experience more powerful and real. Consider this when you watch the perfomance.

9371.belief: In 'Small Island' England is presented as a bad place and Jamaica as a good place.
9371.statement: In 'Small Island' England is presented as a bad place and Jamaica as a good place.
9371.correction: Look at what is happening at the start of Scene 6, why is the situation volatile? What does the discussion between Gilbert and Elwood reveal about the realities in both Jamaica and England?

11040.belief: Only the women in Act 1 consider marriage almost like a business transaction.
11040.statement: That only the women in Act 1 consider marriage almost like a business transaction.
11040.correction: What does Gilbert gain from his marriage to Hortense? How does he describe his feelings towards Hortense and what does this tell the audience?

3046.belief: A flawed character is someone who is always unlikeable or hard to relate to.
3046.statement: A flawed character is someone who is always unlikeable or hard to relate to.
3046.correction: In reality, flawed characters often have human weaknesses that make them more believable or even sympathetic, much like the character of Hortense.

11024.belief: The Windrush generation entered Britain illegally.
11024.statement: The Windrush generation entered Britain illegally.
11024.correction: Those coming from the British Commonwealth were considered citizens.

10671.belief: You should not use your own opinions or perspectives when exploring a text.
10671.statement: That you should not use your own opinions or perspectives when exploring a text.
10671.correction: Being able to articulate your own opinions and perspectives is an important skill to have. They should be rooted in evidence from the text and should avoid speculation.

3533.correction: Think about the promises and expectations that were used to encourage migration. View Hortense's and Gilbert's interaction in light of this betrayal.

3042.belief: The fixed setting in Act 2 means the play is less interesting or creative.
3042.statement: The fixed setting in Act 2 means the play is less interesting or creative.
3042.correction: The fixed setting in Act 2 shows how the characters feel trapped or confined by their situations, which makes the story more powerful and emotional.

2588.belief: Edmundson reveals that dreams are futile and hopeless.
2588.statement: That Edmundson reveals that dreams are futile and hopeless.
2588.correction: Examine the purpose of the idealistic view of England, what does it allow Hortense and Gilbert to do? What reaction do these moments of humour and hope have on the audience?

3299.belief: Gilbert shouting at Hortense shows he doesn’t respect her or care about their relationship.
3299.statement: Gilbert shouting at Hortense shows he doesn’t respect her or care about their relationship
3299.correction: Gilbert’s anger reflects his frustration and the pressures he faces in a racist society. His harsh words mask his deep care and protectiveness, and the scene later shows their developing understanding and connection.

631.belief: Bernard completely rejects Queenie's baby due to his racial prejudices.
631.statement: Bernard completely rejects Queenie's baby due to his racial prejudices.
631.correction: What does the baby symbolise? How does Edmundson use Benard's behaviour to hint at the potential for reparation and change.

9372.belief: 'Small Island' finishes with a perfect resolution.
9372.statement: That 'Small Island' finishes with a perfect resolution.
9372.correction: What issues are addressed in these scenes? Is Edmundson suggesting that these have all been solved? Why is the theme of hope so important?

634.belief: The best endings are always neat and fully resolved, tying up every storyline.
634.statement: The best endings are always neat and fully resolved, tying up every storyline.
634.correction: While neat endings can feel satisfying, 'Small Island' shows powerful endings often include uncertainty. Edmundson says the play balances hope and love with an unclear future, making it realistic and thought-provoking.

2407.belief: The director just tells the actors where to stand and how to say their lines.
2407.statement: The director just tells the actors where to stand and how to say their lines.
2407.correction: According to Norris, that’s only the simplest description. A director also creates an atmosphere of confidence, supports actors, makes key creative decisions, and ensures the whole production comes together smoothly.

3531.correction: Look at how many scenes other characters are in and the importance of their journeys. Why might Levy choose to have multiple protagonists? Think back to her original intentions.

2653.belief: The ending is happy because everything works out perfectly and offers hope for the future.
2653.statement: The ending is happy because everything works out perfectly and offers hope for the future.
2653.correction: Edmundson says the ending is hopeful, but not perfect. There’s pain, loss, and compromise (Queenie gives up her baby), but real progress comes from facing reality with care and honesty.

5549.belief: Planning is not something that needs to be practiced.
5549.statement: That planning is not something that needs to be practiced.
5549.correction: What are the benefits of practising planning over writing whole essay responses? Not only is planning a very important part of the writing process, but an efficient way to practise essay writing.

5538.belief: Planning is not necessary to write an effective response.
5538.statement: Planning is not necessary to write an effective response.
5538.correction: Not only is planning an efficient way to consider different questions and arguments, it also leads to more cohesive, well sequenced responses.

2016.belief: Context refers only to historical facts.
2016.statement: That context refers only to historical facts.
2016.correction: Interesting context also includes different attitudes and values. How would different audiences respond to the text and why?

3849.correction: An effective introduction means you can impress your reader from the outset and clearly layout your overarching argument for your essay.

4446.belief: Many students often think that planning isn't a useful step in the writing process and that it takes too long.
4446.statement: Many students often think that planning isn't a useful step in the writing process and that it takes too long.
4446.correction: How might planning help to organise our thoughts into a coherent response? How can planning improve the efficiency of the writing process?

5081.belief: Once an essay is completed it's not worth thinking about again.
5081.statement: Once an essay is completed it's not worth thinking about again.
5081.correction: How does rewriting support the writing of future responses? Consider the strategies, tips and phrases explored. Revisiting our own essays can make feedback become really personalised and allow you to work and focus on your own targets.

8764.belief: We would react the same way towards the characters and events as would the Jacobean audience.
8764.statement: We would react the same way towards the characters and events as would the Jacobean audience.
8764.correction: Explain that societal beliefs were different in the 1600s so a Jacobean audience would likely react differently to the events and characters

10373.belief: A tragedy is simply a sad play.
10373.statement: A tragedy is simply a sad play.
10373.correction: Tragedies have specific conventions, such as a tragic hero and their hamartia, a tragic fall and elements of fate or the supernatural.

9236.belief: Shakespeare wrote only according to Aristotle's notion of tragedy.
9236.statement: Shakespeare wrote only according to Aristotle's notion of tragedy.
9236.correction: Shakespeare had his own beliefs about tragedy and combined them with Aristotle's ideas.

9238.belief: Shakespearean tragic heroes are often nobility who command respect from all before their fall.
9238.statement: Shakespearean tragic heroes are often nobility who command respect from all before their fall.
9238.correction: Othello, the tragic hero, is not respected by Iago and Roderigo because of his race.

3572.belief: Iago is simply a villain - unkind and evil.
3572.statement: Iago is simply a villain - unkind and evil.
3572.correction: Iago's character as a villain can be looked at through different lenses. One is Machiavellian.

5264.belief: Othello will live up to others' expectations and opinions of him.
5264.statement: Othello will live up to others' expectations and opinions of him.
5264.correction: Othello is completely different to other's perceptions of him. Indeed, he must be worthy of sympathy if he is to be a tragic hero.

10356.belief: Topic sentences are not worth spending much time on, the discussion of techniques is more important.
10356.statement: Topic sentences are not worth spending much time on, the discussion of techniques is more important.
10356.correction: To make a paragraph even more effective, a topic sentence can be elevated in many ways to make writing clear and specific with a firm voice.

9627.belief: The storm in Othello is just a device that means the Turkish army is defeated and the war is over.
9627.statement: The storm in Othello is just a device that means the Turkish army is defeated and the war is over.
9627.correction: The storm in Othello is a device that is symbolic of chaos and disorder to come.

3571.belief: Iago is similar to many other Shakespeare villains.
3571.statement: Iago is similar to many other Shakespeare villains.
3571.correction: Iago stands out because of his diabolical nature.

5136.belief: Only one interpretation of Iago is relevant since he is clearly a villain.
5136.statement: Only one interpretation of Iago is relevant since he is clearly a villain.
5136.correction: Even villains can be looked at through multiple lenses. Doing this can elevate your response as you say what others may not consider.

5265.belief: Othello's downfall is solely due to his own faults.
5265.statement: Othello's downfall is solely due to his own faults.
5265.correction: Shakespeare carefully crafts Iago as someone who plays a huge role in Othello's downfall - acting like the serpent in the Garden of Eden.

501.belief: The audience will perceive the tragic hero to be at complete fault for their downfall.
501.statement: The audience will perceive the tragic hero to be at complete fault for their downfall.
501.correction: In Othello, due to the amount of time we spend getting to know Iago, we can see the huge role Iago plays in Othello's character change.

3570.belief: Iago is an evil villain, completely in control the whole play.
3570.statement: Iago is an evil villain, completely in control the whole play.
3570.correction: Iago begins to show his fallibility in 5.1.

2273.belief: Desdemona conforms to Jacobean stereotypes throughout the play.
2273.statement: Desdemona conforms to Jacobean stereotypes throughout the play.
2273.correction: Desdemona's character changes throughout the play - it is only at the end that she seems to conform.

5262.belief: Othello is the only character that suffers a tragic fate.
5262.statement: Othello is the only character that suffers a tragic fate
5262.correction: Desdemona, Emilia and Othello all suffer a tragic fate

5266.belief: Othello's jealousy is the only thing that causes him to be considered a tragic hero.
5266.statement: Othello's jealousy is the only thing that causes him to be considered a tragic hero.
5266.correction: Othello also has hubris, stubbornness and anagnorisis that can add to his status as tragic hero.

2747.belief: An essay can contain random ideas about a theme/character as long as they link to the question.
2747.statement: An essay can contain random ideas about a theme/character as long as they link to the question.
2747.correction: Points in an essay should be planned tightly to expand upon and demonstrate the thesis statement.

2748.belief: An essay is effective as long as it contains a range of evidence.
2748.statement: An essay is effective as long as it contains a range of evidence.
2748.correction: To maximise effectiveness of an essay, you should link pieces of evidence together.

4726.belief: Motifs and symbols are the same.
4726.statement: Motifs and symbols are the same.
4726.correction: A motif is a recurring image whereas a symbol is one thing that represents something else.

5261.belief: Othello acts in the way he does simply due to his hamartia: jealousy.
5261.statement: Othello acts in the way he does simply due to his hamartia: jealousy.
5261.correction: We must interrogate why Othello is targeted by Iago, how his outsider status makes him more susceptible to manipulation and insecurity.

2015.belief: Context just needs to be included in a response to make it effective.
2015.statement: Context just needs to be included in a response to make it effective.
2015.correction: Context must not only be included but carefully considered, adapted and moulded to the point you are trying to make.

341.belief: Appearance vs. reality is only shown through Othello believing his wife is unfaithful.
341.statement: Appearance vs. reality is only shown through Othello believing his wife is unfaithful.
341.correction: There are many moments in the play in which appearance and reality are manipulated

4270.belief: As long as you have planned the argument of your essay, you are ready to write it.
4270.statement: As long as you have planned the argument of your essay, you are ready to write it.
4270.correction: Planning topic sentences to go with your argument is also important to ensure that your essay is focused on proving the argument.

5263.belief: Only Othello feels jealousy in the play.
5263.statement: Only Othello feels jealousy in the play.
5263.correction: Many other characters feel jealousy and it is a driving force for lots of the action in the play.

2018.belief: Context is separate to ideas and analysis.
2018.statement: Context is separate to ideas and analysis.
2018.correction: Context is not an add on for an essay, it is something that can shape arguments.

5657.belief: Poems and song lyrics are the same.
5657.statement: Poems and song lyrics are the same.
5657.correction: While there are similarities, Armitage suggests that poems have to create musicality through language while song lyrics are a component of a larger whole.

11159.belief: Writing is purely a form of escapism.
11159.statement: Writing is purely a form of escapism.
11159.correction: For some, writing can be a way of helping to process emotions and ideas.

667.belief: A biography offers an authentic impression of that person.
667.statement: A biography offers an authentic impression of that person.
667.correction: We all might have different perspectives on the same person, so different biographies are likely to portray the same person in different ways.

5666.belief: Poetry about a personal event should be as emotional as possible.
5666.statement: Poetry about a personal event should be as emotional as possible.
5666.correction: Armitage suggests that poetry about personal events should convey emotion without being too obvious or too sentimental.

5624.belief: A poem is completely separate from a narrative story.
5624.statement: A poem is completely separate from a narrative story.
5624.correction: Fundamentally, a poem is about the manipulation of language - so you can manipulate a narrative story into a poem.

5635.belief: A poem about those who have lost their lives will always be sad.
5635.statement: A poem about those who have lost their lives will always be sad.
5635.correction: While laments for the dead contain sadness, they also often contain elements of hope and joy for the lives lived and the futures ahead.

8775.belief: Reading a poem aloud is the same as reading prose aloud.
8775.statement: Reading a poem aloud is the same as reading prose aloud.
8775.correction: When reading a poem, you need to consider the line breaks in a way that you don't have to with prose.

10451.belief: You should try to speak for other people in your writing.
10451.statement: You should try to speak for other people in your writing.
10451.correction: We all have slightly different opinions and ideas, so you should try to communicate your ideas and emotions to other people through your writing.

5047.belief: You should be objective when you are writing about world events.
5047.statement: You should be objective when you are writing about world events.
5047.correction: Armitage suggests that poetry is about the individual and that we have a responsibility to reflect our personal responses to what's happening in the world.

5663.belief: Poetic language does not exist in everyday life.
5663.statement: Poetic language does not exist in everyday life.
5663.correction: Poetic language is everywhere since we use metaphors and comparisons in everyday speech all the time.

756.correction: Brod is a family friend. Enid's husband is mentioned in the play, but he left her and his two children when they were little.

5582.belief: The play is only about the past or historical events.
5582.statement: The play is only about the past or historical events.
5582.correction: Pinnock emphasises that the play connects past and present. It explores immigrant experiences, cultural identity, and family relationships, showing issues that are still relevant today.

11025.belief: The Windrush generation were illegal migrants.
11025.statement: The Windrush generation were illegal migrants.
11025.correction: Those coming from the British Commonwealth were considered citizens.

2690.belief: Enid doesn't think England is racist.
2690.statement: Enid doesn't think England is racist.
2690.correction: Enid is very private about her views: we see only her reaction to the discrimination she faces. Consider if her dialogue reveals more.

5838.belief: Each production of a play is the same because the play's script is always the same.
5838.statement: Each production of a play is the same because the play's script is always the same.
5838.correction: The production of a play is always unique. The choice of director, producer, theatre, cast and the nature of its audiences all contribute.

4087.belief: 'Leave Taking' was written about the Windrush scandal.
4087.statement: 'Leave Taking' was written about the Windrush scandal.
4087.correction: Pinnock explains that she wrote 'Leave Taking' decades before the Windrush scandal, but some themes, like the precarious position of immigrants, happened to resonate with contemporary events when the play was revived.

758.correction: Consider the admiration Brod has for Pastor Chully Johnson.

2693.belief: Enid's husband never loved her. They had a terrible relationship.
2693.statement: Enid's husband never loved her. They had a terrible relationship.
2693.correction: Whilst there are descriptions of conflict in their relationship, the description of their moving to England shows their initial devotion.

2225.belief: Del is as rude as ever about obeah.
2225.statement: Del is as rude as ever about obeah.
2225.correction: Del is rude in this scene, but she also asks questions and watches Mai's practices.

2224.belief: Del hates the education system and school.
2224.statement: Del hates the education system and school.
2224.correction: Whilst Del did not have a positive school experience, she knows the value of education, hence her extreme reaction to Viv skipping an exam.

4360.correction: Mai's son was born in Britain, but his cultural identity is important to him and he doesn't feel at home in Britain.

759.belief: Brod's drinking is appropriate and meant to be funny.
759.statement: Brod's drinking is appropriate and meant to be funny.
759.correction: Both Enid and Del challenge Brod's drinking, and his scenes expose his unhappiness, isolation and vulnerability.

5586.belief: The play is set over a series of days so Del's character development is rapid.
5586.statement: The play is set over a series of days so Del's character development is rapid.
5586.correction: The stage directions at the beginning of each scene show that sometimes a few days have past, and sometimes much longer.

2691.belief: Enid and other immigrants came to Britain fully aware of the challenges and were prepared for discrimination.
2691.statement: Enid and other immigrants came to Britain fully aware of the challenges and were prepared for discrimination.
2691.correction: Pinnock explains that many, like Enid, saw themselves as British subjects and expected a “homecoming”, so the hostility and racism they faced were a shock.

2694.belief: Enid's life in Jamaica was terrible. It wasn't hard for her to leave.
2694.statement: Enid's life in Jamaica was terrible. It wasn't hard for her to leave.
2694.correction: Enid faced limited opportunities in Jamaica, but leaving also meant she forever altered her relationships with her family and community.

5746.belief: The poverty Enid faced in Jamaica is equivalent to the poverty she faces in England.
5746.statement: The poverty Enid faced in Jamaica is equivalent to the poverty she faces in England.
5746.correction: Enid faced rural poverty where she "lived off the land". Farming is unreliable, and her family could feasibly become destitute.

833.belief: You can't analyse stage directions in depth.
833.statement: You can't analyse stage directions in depth.
833.correction: The closing stage directions of 'Leave Taking' are integral in understanding Pinnock's final messages about the characters and themes.

2226.belief: Del is uninterested in obeah until Mai realises it is her calling.
2226.statement: Del is uninterested in obeah until Mai realises it is her calling.
2226.correction: Del's interest in obeah is foreshadowed from Scene One onwards.

755.belief: Brod contrasts Enid in every way.
755.statement: Brod contrasts Enid in every way.
755.correction: Brod and Enid clash over education, Jamaica and England, but they also have many commonalities: their past and their migration.

4359.belief: Mai's desire that people "invest" in themselves is just a way for her to make more money.
4359.statement: Mai's desire that people "invest" in themselves is just a way for her to make more money.
4359.correction: Whilst Mai is determined to be paid for her services, she takes her calling seriously.

2692.belief: Enid wants to move back to Jamaica.
2692.statement: Enid wants to move back to Jamaica.
2692.correction: Enid is full of inner conflict; it is not as simple as wanting to move back to Jamaica, or wanting to stay in England.

10237.belief: Thesis statements and topic sentences are synonymous.
10237.statement: Thesis statements and topic sentences are synonymous.
10237.correction: Thesis statements are supported by the whole text. Topic sentences give direction and purpose to individual paragraphs.

8728.belief: Every quotation you write about should be analysed in detail.
8728.statement: Every quotation you write about should be analysed in detail.
8728.correction: Main quotations should be analysed, but you should also include supporting quotations that are embedded into sentences without analysis.

2014.belief: Context must be included in every paragraph.
2014.statement: Context must be included in every paragraph.
2014.correction: Context must be included in essays, but where it is relevant and develops your analysis - not as a tick box exercise for each paragraph.

1912.belief: Concluding sentences are the same as conclusions.
1912.statement: Concluding sentences are the same as conclusions.
1912.correction: Concluding sentences conclude a single paragraph. Conclusions come at the end of a full essay.

3223.belief: The general statement about the text in the introduction can be any fact you know about it.
3223.statement: The general statement about the text in the introduction can be any fact you know about it.
3223.correction: The general statement, the first sentence of your introduction, should still connect to the essay question.

2466.belief: You don't need to plan topic sentences in full.
2466.statement: You don't need to plan topic sentences in full.
2466.correction: Write topic sentences in full when planning. They give the essay structure and make sure you develop and support your thesis.

5542.belief: All planning should be in note form.
5542.statement: All planning should be in note form.
5542.correction: Foundations of your essay - thesis and topic sentences - should be written in full so you know they are powerful, precise and purposeful.

2010.belief: Context can't be included in a topic sentence or analysis. It must be confined to its own sentences.
2010.statement: Context can't be included in a topic sentence or analysis. It must be confined to its own sentences.
2010.correction: Context can be woven into any moment in a paragraph; you must decide where it will be most purposeful.

1779.belief: Any comments about a writer's intentions or choices must be absolute.
1779.statement: Any comments about a writer's intentions or choices must be absolute.
1779.correction: Although we may never know for certain, we can use clues like contextual information to develop ideas around intentions and choices. We can also use tentative language to put forward our ideas.

9392.belief: Social responsibility means just helping those in need.
9392.statement: Social responsibility means just helping those in need.
9392.correction: Social responsibility is about considering the impact of our actions on others and society, not just charity. It involves accountability for our role in social issues, like inequality.

250.belief: When analysing a play, you only focus on the characters' dialogue.
250.statement: When analysing a play, you only focus on the characters' dialogue.
250.correction: Stage directions can provide a lot of clues around the writer's intention and vision. They also offer an understanding of charcaterisation.

5583.belief: If a play is not resolved or offers a clear conclusion it is not effective and just feels uncomfortable for the audience.
5583.statement: If a play is not resolved or offers a clear conclusion it is not effective and just feels uncomfortable for the audience.
5583.correction: Arguably, this is what the writer wants you to feel with an ambiguous ending. An unresolved ending may provoke more questions and be used by the writer to make a point.

5119.belief: There is always one clear and deifnite interpretation of a charcater.
5119.statement: There is always one clear and deifnite interpretation of a charcater.
5119.correction: Characters can have multiple interpretations based on context, perspective, and evidence in the text. Writers like Priestley create complex characters to provoke debate and reflection.

3870.belief: Isn't the fact that Mr. Birling wants to look after himself and his family a good thing?
3870.statement: Isn't the fact that Mr. Birling wants to look after himself and his family a good thing?
3870.correction: It's understandable to think that Mr. Birling's focus on looking after himself and his family could be seen as positive. However, Priestley shows that Mr. Birling's attitude is self-serving and dismissive of wider societal responsibilities.

4749.belief: Mrs. Birling’s interrogation shows her changing attitude towards responsibility.
4749.statement: Mrs. Birling’s interrogation shows her changing attitude towards responsibility.
4749.correction: Although Mrs. Birling has some revelations about her family towards the end of Act 2, her attitude remains unchanged at the end of the play. She stubbornly refuses to accept any responsibility, reinforcing her commitment to class prejudices.

9255.correction: While her growth is significant, it doesn't ensure broader social progress, as societal norms and traditions play a major role.

2599.belief: An effective essay includes all of your thoughts on the subject.
2599.statement: An effective essay includes all of your thoughts on the subject.
2599.correction: An effective essay is structured cohesively rather than including every thought.

2735.belief: Eric’s guilt makes him fully sympathetic.
2735.statement: Eric’s guilt makes him fully sympathetic.
2735.correction: Eric's actions and narrative can still be challenged. For example, his attempts to downplay his responsibility may show his moral flaws.

3243.belief: Gerald's actions are based entirely on kindess and he did a good thing in supporting Eva.
3243.statement: Gerald's actions are based entirely on kindess and he did a good thing in supporting Eva.
3243.correction: Gerald’s actions may seem kind, but they are driven by self-interest and privilege. He offers Eva financial support, but it is not out of pure kindness—he uses his power to control her, ultimately exploiting her for his own benefit.

8729.belief: All quotations in an essay require analysis.
8729.statement: All quotations in an essay require analysis.
8729.correction: Some quotations are useful for supporting your argument but do not require detailed analysis. These should embedded directly into pupils' sentences.

9556.belief: Spending too much time reading the question wastes time when you could be writing the essay.
9556.statement: Spending too much time reading the question wastes time when you could be writing the essay.
9556.correction: Spending time reading the question allows us to select what is relevant. It is just as important to know what not to include in a well argued response.

3242.correction: Although Orwell wanted an equal society, he viewed communism as corruptible and idealistic.

297.belief: The animals are always equal, even from the very start.
297.statement: That the animals are always equal, even from the very start.
297.correction: Focus on the positioning of the animals and how they enter the barn. Orwell is already beginning to make distinctions between the animals.

5066.correction: The three pigs invent Animalism in response to Old Major's speech. What might Orwell be commenting on here or trying to reveal?

5519.belief: The pigs immediately set about taking control of the farm.
5519.statement: The pigs immediately set about taking control of the farm.
5519.correction: The pigs' increasing power and control is a gradual process, relying on incremental changes in the commandments to gain overall control.

298.belief: All animals were equally responsible for the defence of Animal Farm.
298.statement: All animals were equally responsible for the defence of Animal Farm.
298.correction: Snowball and Boxer were instrumental in the victory. Mollie deliberately shied away and Napoleon was curiously unmentioned.

4815.belief: Napoleon's move towards autocracy is a sudden process.
4815.statement: Napoleon's move towards autocracy is a sudden process.
4815.correction: It is gradual. Each chapter sees the spirit of the revolution and 'Animalism' further degraded by the actions of Napoleon and the pigs.

303.belief: The animals are happy in the work and with the sacrifices they are making.
303.statement: That the animals are happy in the work and with the sacrifices they are making.
303.correction: Link back to Orwell's purpose about manipulation and propaganda. Their reality does not match the promises of the revolution.

9383.belief: Snowball really is responsible for the windmill collapsing and other events on the farm.
9383.statement: That Snowball really is responsible for the windmill collapsing and other events on the farm.
9383.correction: Explore the question, how do you know if propaganda is working effectively? When there is unwavering belief in its messages.

294.belief: The animals' apparent support for the pigs is genuine loyalty.
294.statement: The animals' apparent support for the pigs is genuine loyalty.
294.correction: The reality is that this is manipulation, fear, and the pigs' gradual control over them. Examine the pigs' tactics.

307.belief: The animals could not have stopped the revolution.
307.statement: That the animals could not have stopped the revolution.
307.correction: How does Orwell describe Boxer? He is physically powerful and commands respect. If he had intelligence could he have made a difference?

8934.belief: The revolution is a complete failure.
8934.statement: That the revolution is a complete failure.
8934.correction: Explore the quote "the farm was more prosperous now, and better organised". Who has benefitted? Would some consider this a success?

627.belief: Benjamin is a minor character in 'Animal Farm' and doesn't represent much.
627.statement: Benjamin is a minor character in 'Animal Farm' and doesn't represent much.
627.correction: Could Benjamin make a difference? Could he have used his intelligence? Benjamin's apathy has a key role in the pigs' reign.

300.belief: The animals feel negatively towards the rituals and ideas put forward by the pigs.
300.statement: That the animals feel negatively towards the rituals and ideas put forward by the pigs.
300.correction: Think about the response to Beasts of England. Is this same atmosphere created by Napoleon's parade? Why are the pigs' rituals different?

4814.belief: Napoleon and Old Major are completely different.
4814.statement: That Napoleon and Old Major are completely different.
4814.correction: Look closely at their speeches. Interestingly they are very similar in their uses of devices, delivery and how they motivate the animals.

3340.statement: That there are "good" pigs and "bad" pigs.
3340.correction: For Orwell, all are susceptible to power and corruption. Orwell uses the pigs to critique the subtle and overt ways that this can be done.

2821.belief: Everyone in power sees education as a way to better society.
2821.statement: That everyone in power sees education as a way to better society.
2821.correction: How does it feel when you don't understand something? Confusing? Scary? Disorientating? How could the pigs use this to their advantage?

5252.belief: Orwell offers a solution to the problems he explores.
5252.statement: Orwell offers a solution to the problems he explores.
5252.correction: Explore the idea of "resolution" in terms of 'Animal Farm'. Does Orwell offer any resolutions? Does the story feel finished?

8734.statement: That quotes need to be long.
8734.correction: Explore the purpose of quotes and how efficiency is key. What is considered an effective use of quotes?

5253.belief: Orwell offers a solution to the problems he highlights.
5253.statement: That Orwell offers a solution to the problems he highlights.
5253.correction: Focus on the cyclical structure and lack of resolution. How does this reflect Orwell's purpose? Is he just being critical and cynical?

5550.correction: A detailed plan will speed up the writing process and ensure a cohesive and well structured argument.

3848.correction: An effective introduction and conclusion means that a written response is more likely to be well considered and cohesive throughout.

621.belief: There is no benefit in looking at other people's responses.
621.statement: There is no benefit in looking at other people's responses.
621.correction: How do you feel looking at your own work? It is quite difficult to be critical of your own work, practising on model essays helps this.

8733.belief: Quotes in essays need to be long and are difficult to remember.
8733.statement: That quotes in essays need to be long and are difficult to remember.
8733.correction: Can you remember anything Boxer says? How about words used to describe characters? Any of the commandments? These are all key quotes.

3343.belief: Good vs. evil is easy to recognise in characters when reading stories or watching plays.
3343.statement: That good vs. evil is easy to recognise in characters when reading stories or watching plays.
3343.correction: In tragedies, sometimes a character can embody both good and evil or there could be different perceptions of a character's nature.

2793.belief: Everyone believes they have control over their lives.
2793.statement: That everyone believes they have control over their lives.
2793.correction: Some people believe that their lives are controlled by fate and destiny.

3932.belief: Juliet is Romeo's only love in 'Romeo and Juliet'.
3932.statement: That Juliet is Romeo's only love in 'Romeo and Juliet'.
3932.correction: Before meeting Juliet, Romeo was in love with Rosaline.

11049.belief: Women were slaves in patriarchal societies.
11049.statement: That women were slaves in patriarchal societies.
11049.correction: While women had less legal power in patriarchal societies, they could still be very influential and powerful.

2800.belief: Everyone in Elizabethan England thought dreams were profound and important.
2800.statement: That everyone in Elizabethan England thought dreams were profound and important.
2800.correction: Mercutio's 'Queen Mab' speech implies that dreams are inconsequential and merely wish-fulfillment.

9012.belief: Romeo and Juliet's first conversation exclusively focuses on the physicality of their love.
9012.statement: That Romeo and Juliet's first conversation exclusively focuses on the physicality of their love.
9012.correction: While Romeo and Juliet's first conversation contains many references to "lips" and "palms", the religious imagery also implies their spiritual connection.

9011.belief: Romeo is more impulsive than Juliet in Shakespeare's 'Romeo and Juliet'.
9011.statement: Romeo is more impulsive than Juliet in Shakespeare's 'Romeo and Juliet'.
9011.correction: Arguably, Juliet's actions are also impulsive.

3933.belief: Juliet was Romeo's only love in Shakespeare's 'Romeo and Juliet'.
3933.statement: Juliet was Romeo's only love in Shakespeare's 'Romeo and Juliet'.
3933.correction: Before Juliet, Romeo believes himself to be in love with Rosaline.

5403.belief: People in Elizabethan England share the same ideas about religion as we do in modern society.
5403.statement: That people in Elizabethan England share the same ideas about religion as we do in modern society.
5403.correction: Religion was central to people's lives in Elizabethan England in a way that it is not in modern society.

8990.belief: The role of comedy is merely to make people laugh.
8990.statement: The role of comedy is merely to make people laugh.
8990.correction: Comedy can be a way of revealing information about characters.

9013.belief: Romeo is often said to be 'in love with love' and this is consistent throughout the play.
9013.statement: Romeo is often said to be 'in love with love' and this is consistent throughout the play.
9013.correction: In Act 3, Scene 1, Romeo expresses negative feelings towards the concept of being in love.

4152.belief: Light always symbolises hope and optimism in literature.
4152.statement: That light always symbolises hope and optimism in literature.
4152.correction: While light typically symbolises hope and optimism, for Romeo and Juliet it symbolises loss and separation.

948.belief: Characters either fully conform or fully subvert stereotypes.
948.statement: That characters either fully conform or fully subvert stereotypes.
948.correction: Characters often exist within a grey area - they might conform to some aspects of a stereotype but subvert others - just as real people do.

5406.belief: People generally believe in free will and always have.
5406.statement: That people generally believe in free will and always have.
5406.correction: In Elizabethan England, people typically believed that fate controlled their lives - they believed they did not have free will.

3593.belief: Just identifying a method in a quotation is effective.
3593.statement: That just identifying a method in a quotation is effective.
3593.correction: To be effective, you need to analyse the effect of the method in the quotation.

4327.correction: 'Macbeth' is set in 11th century Scotland. However, it was first performed in 1606 in front of a Jacobean audience.

4332.belief: The Macbeths invite Duncan to their castle so they can kill him.
4332.statement: The Macbeths invite Duncan to their castle so they can kill him.
4332.correction: King Duncan is honouring the Macbeths by staying with them; he is honouring them because of Macbeth's performance in the recent battle.

4326.correction: Shakespeare signals the dagger is a hallucination, and that Macbeth is aware it is a hallucination too: 'a dagger of the mind'.

4328.belief: Macbeth is next in line to the throne.
4328.statement: Macbeth is next in line to the throne.
4328.correction: Malcolm has been named Duncan's heir. However, he flees to England and thus Macbeth is crowned King.

4330.belief: Macbeth is solely worried about Banquo and Fleance in this scene.
4330.statement: Macbeth is solely worried about Banquo and Fleance in this scene.
4330.correction: Macbeth's focus is Banquo and his son, but his language reveals his worries about the regicide, his soul and his immediate future.

4331.belief: Macbeth is a tyrannical ruler, and enjoys his tyranny.
4331.statement: Macbeth is a tyrannical ruler, and enjoys his tyranny.
4331.correction: Macbeth is a tyrant, but doesn't enjoy his reign. He is also self-aware: "I am in blood Stepp'd so far" or calling the witches "the worst".

4394.correction: Malcolm pretends he is filled with lust and greed, but this is to test Macduff's loyalty.

3625.belief: The imaginary blood on Lady Macbeth's hands could symbolise Duncan's blood.
3625.statement: The imaginary blood on Lady Macbeth's hands could symbolise Duncan's blood.
3625.correction: Symbols represent an idea that doesn't have a physical existence. Guilt is not a physical thing so the object, blood, is used.

10223.belief: A theme is any moment or idea in a text.
10223.statement: A theme is any moment or idea in a text.
10223.correction: A theme is an idea that is explored in multiple different ways - it has to come up more than once in a text.

3032.belief: The first scene is an exciting spectacle but not important to the rest of the play.
3032.statement: The first scene is an exciting spectacle but not important to the rest of the play.
3032.correction: Despite its length, this scene grounds us in the atmosphere and main themes of the play.

11036.belief: The witches are presented solely as women, threatening women but women nonetheless.
11036.statement: The witches are presented solely as women, threatening women but women nonetheless.
11036.correction: Look at the language in Act 1, Scene 3: Banquo and Macbeth see the witches as unnatural, not just strange women.

11035.belief: The witches are presented in one way; any new interpretation supersedes the one before.
11035.statement: The witches are presented in one way; any new interpretation supersedes the one before.
11035.correction: The witches are presented as supernatural, women, masculine and genderless. Paragraphs can explore all these; rely on LC2 to draw this out.

4005.belief: Lady Macbeth's 'unsex me' here means she wants to be a man.
4005.statement: Lady Macbeth's 'unsex me' here means she wants to be a man.
4005.correction: Whilst she might want some masculine qualities, there are more implications to this. She could be calling for supernatural qualities too.

5152.belief: There is just one reason that Macbeth doesn't want to commit regicide - his loyalty to Duncan.
5152.statement: There is just one reason that Macbeth doesn't want to commit regicide - his loyalty to Duncan.
5152.correction: Macbeth's soliloquy explores crime but significantly earthly punishment. For Macbeth, the consequence on earth is what frightens him.

4003.belief: Lady Macbeth's presentation is the same in both Act 1, Scene 5 and Scene 7.
4003.statement: Lady Macbeth's presentation is the same in both Act 1, Scene 5 and Scene 7.
4003.correction: There is an increase in urgency, violence and strategy in Act 1, Scene 7.

4002.correction: Lady Macbeth does value loyalty, but loyalty to herself and her ambitions, not the chivalric code.

374.belief: The only argument about Lady Macbeth involves her being subversive.
374.statement: The only argument about Lady Macbeth involves her being subversive.
374.correction: Characters can be interpreted in different ways. Your role is to construct a strong argument, not the 'right' argument.

4004.belief: Lady Macbeth's rejection of guilt in 2.2 means 5.1's characterisation is inconsistent.
4004.statement: Lady Macbeth's rejection of guilt in 2.2 means 5.1's characterisation is inconsistent.
4004.correction: The language in 2.2 foreshadows what is to come.

4762.belief: The murder of Banquo and Fleance (attempted) is the same as the murders that have preceded it.
4762.statement: The murder of Banquo and Fleance (attempted) is the same as the murders that have preceded it.
4762.correction: Macbeth doesn't tell Lady Macbeth his plan, he hires murderers rather than doing it himself, and Fleance is a child.

548.belief: Banquo's ghost is definitely a figment of Macbeth's imagination.
548.statement: Banquo's ghost is definitely a figment of Macbeth's imagination.
548.correction: It's up to directors whether Banquo's ghost should appear on stage; an actor could play this part, or Macbeth could be scared of nothing.

4001.belief: Lady Macbeth doesn't think guilt is a powerful emotion.
4001.statement: Lady Macbeth doesn't think guilt is a powerful emotion.
4001.correction: Lady Macbeth acknowledges that guilt can make people 'mad' or 'brainsickly' in 2.2. This is why she tries to reject the emotion.

3439.belief: Hamartia is a synonym for excessive ambition.
3439.statement: Hamartia is a synonym for excessive ambition.
3439.correction: Consider if students have read any other tragedies. Ask them to consider Othello's hamartia, for example.

9235.belief: Shakespeare was a misogynist or, conversely, Shakespeare was a feminist.
9235.statement: Shakespeare was a misogynist or, conversely, Shakespeare was a feminist.
9235.correction: We don't know about Shakespeare's political or social beliefs. The text is there for us to interpret, not define Shakespeare's views.

10238.belief: Thesis and topic sentences are the same thing.
10238.statement: Thesis and topic sentences are the same thing.
10238.correction: A thesis must be overarching. A topic sentence can be much more specific.

258.belief: Analysis can only include a language focus, especially single word analysis.
258.statement: Analysis can only include a language focus, especially single word analysis.
258.correction: You should analyse a range of writer's methods; this analysis should support your thesis or topic sentence.

2021.belief: Contextual information in an essay should comprise of one final sentence in each paragraph.
2021.statement: Contextual information in an essay should comprise of one final sentence in each paragraph.
2021.correction: Context should be weaved throughout an essay to help explore a writer's intentions.

9954.belief: "third person limited" means the narrative is limited in scope or detail.
9954.statement: Students might think that "third person limited" means the narrative is limited in scope or detail.
9954.correction: "Third person limited" means insight into one character's thoughts, not a story's limited scope.

9628.belief: The story takes place in a dark, gloomy and traditionally Gothic setting.
9628.statement: The story takes place in a dark, gloomy and traditionally Gothic setting.
9628.correction: Stevenson deliberately juxtaposes the building Hyde enters with the pleasant and well-to-do neighbourhood.

9948.belief: Stevenson's ambiguity about Hyde's appearance is due to insufficient detail.
9948.statement: Students might think Stevenson's ambiguity about Hyde's appearance is due to insufficient detail.
9948.correction: Stevenson keeps Hyde's description vague to engage readers' imaginations, amplifying the character's eeriness.

7867.belief: The genre of this novella is solely Gothic fiction.
7867.statement: Pupils think the genre of this novella is solely Gothic fiction.
7867.correction: Even without the presence of a detective character, the use of concealment and a carefully crafted mystery make this detective fiction too.

946.belief: Character is more important than setting when trying to solve mystery.
946.statement: Character is more important than setting when trying to solve mystery.
946.correction: Jekyll tells Utterson there is nothing he should worry about - this is not true. Ask pupils how the setting indicates that Jekyll is lying.

10769.belief: Utterson, as a lawyer, is a man of great curiosity and honour.
10769.statement: Utterson, as a lawyer, is a man of great curiosity and honour.
10769.correction: Utterson is both curious for the truth, but cautious about ruining the reputation of his peers. This leads to important clues being missed.

4188.belief: Liminal spaces are things that are unnerving in a mysterious way.
4188.statement: Liminal spaces are things that are unnerving in a mysterious way.
4188.correction: Liminal spaces often do create a unnerving tone, but this is due to them being the boundary to two opposing states.

873.belief: The case is over now Hyde has been found dead.
873.statement: The case is over now Hyde has been found dead.
873.correction: Get students enthused about the final mystery - how has Jekyll disappeared from a room locked from the inside?

943.belief: Chapter 9 takes place after the events in Chapter 8.
943.statement: Chapter 9 takes place after the events in Chapter 8.
943.correction: Ask pupils if they were going to put the chapters in chronological order, how would this chapter be numbered? (Answer: Chapter 6)

2650.belief: The end of Chapter 8 implies Jekyll regretted creating Hyde.
2650.statement: The end of Chapter 8 implies Jekyll regretted creating Hyde.
2650.correction: Jekyll is a very complex character, his actions need to be explored with nuance. The best responses will consider Jekyll's joy and regret.

3477.belief: Henry Jekyll is responsible for the death of Mr. Hyde. Jekyll is the 'self-destroyer.'.
3477.statement: Henry Jekyll is responsible for the death of Mr. Hyde. Jekyll is the 'self-destroyer.'
3477.correction: Hyde uses Jekyll as his protection from the gallows. When Jekyll is no more, it is Hyde who chooses death over punishment.

3911.belief: 'Jekyll and Hyde' is a stereotypically 'Gothic' novella.
3911.statement: 'Jekyll and Hyde' is a stereotypically 'Gothic' novella.
3911.correction: Whilst certain elements of 'Jekyll and Hyde' do follow the conventions of the Gothic, others subvert it.

1657.belief: All Christians were against scientific development.
1657.statement: All Christians were against scientific development.
1657.correction: Within all religions (or groups in society) there will be plurality of thought, including progressive viewpoints.

9613.belief: Stevenson was extremely critical of science.
9613.statement: Stevenson was extremely critical of science.
9613.correction: Stevenson certainly plays on contemporary fears over unfettered scientific development. Whilst his novella could be seen as a criticism of this, the extent to which which Stevenson uses the text as his own personal criticism is arguable.

8726.belief: Any quotation that supports your argument can be used.
8726.statement: Any quotation that supports your argument can be used.
8726.correction: Select a quotation from learning cycle 1, such as "it wasn't like a man" and ask how much pupils could say about the quotation.

3564.belief: Hyde is solely presented as a dangerous character from the start to the end of the novella.
3564.statement: Hyde is solely presented as a dangerous character from the start to the end of the novella.
3564.correction: Through the character of Hyde, and others' interactions with him, we can explore Stevenson's wider cautionary message.

8651.statement: Pupils must work through the text chronologically when selecting supporting evidence.
8651.correction: Pupils need to think of the logical order they should analyse evidence from the text - which section of the novella is strongest at proving their topic sentence?

254.belief: When analysing, all pupils need is a clear viewpoint.
254.statement: When analysing, all pupils need is a clear viewpoint.
254.correction: A clear viewpoint is important, but adding nuance will improve the quality of pupil responses.

3910.belief: Jekyll is the only character responsible for the crimes of Hyde.
3910.statement: Jekyll is the only character responsible for the crimes of Hyde.
3910.correction: A more nuanced understanding of the text explores the complicity of other characters and the decisions they make.

3692.belief: When including 'the impact of the text today' in your conclusion, you just need to explain why the book is still studied today.
3692.statement: When including 'the impact of the text today' in your conclusion, you just need to explain why the book is still studied today.
3692.correction: Ask pupils to 'step outside the text' and think about why themes, characters or moral messages might resonate with readers today.

4570.belief: Just mentioning Stevenson's choices surrounding form and structure is valuable analysis.
4570.statement: Just mentioning Stevenson's choices surrounding form and structure is valuable analysis.
4570.correction: All comments regarding Stevenson's use of form and structure should be tied back to Stevenson's purpose.

9612.belief: Stevenson encourages the reader to be critical of Jekyll due to the dual nature inherent inside of him.
9612.statement: Stevenson encourages the reader to be critical of Jekyll due to the dual nature inherent inside of him.
9612.correction: Stevenson appears to embrace duality, through his rejection of Calvinism and alleged behaviour at university. He is critical of the hypocrisy that arose from those who harboured secrets as a result of duality.

7715.belief: They have to come up with new ideas for each essay question they attempt.
7715.statement: Pupils might think they have to come up with new ideas for each essay question they attempt.
7715.correction: Highlight similarities between the modelled plan on 'hypocrisy' and their own ideas relationing to 'duality'.

10742.belief: Using tentative language makes you sound unsure in your analysis.
10742.statement: Using tentative language makes you sound unsure in your analysis.
10742.correction: Tentative language allows pupils to be more evaluative, exploring alternative viewpoints.

8232.belief: Scrooge keeps his money to himself so that he can spend it on himself.
8232.statement: Pupils think that Scrooge keeps his money to himself so that he can spend it on himself.
8232.correction: Scrooge's frugality also extends to his own existence: Scrooge refuses to spend money even on himself, choosing to live a meagre lifestyle.

9933.belief: Scrooge hates Christmas because it marks the anniversary of Marley's death.
9933.statement: Students think that Scrooge hates Christmas because it marks the anniversary of Marley's death.
9933.correction: Scrooge hates Christmas because he views it as a crime against oneself. He resents that people spend money they don't have at Christmas.

9814.statement: Students often talk about Marley and Marley's Ghost as if they are the exact same character.
9814.correction: Marley in life held very different beliefs from Marley's ghost; his ghost acts as Scrooge's redeemer and represents something different.

9936.belief: Scrooge is just a wicked character who hates other people, especially the poor.
9936.statement: Students think Scrooge is just a wicked character who hates other people, especially the poor.
9936.correction: Scrooge is a product of his environment and exemplifies the attitudes of many Victorian employers and wealthy citizens.

9813.statement: Students do not take the time to plan properly before writing.
9813.correction: Not taking the time to plan a response properly makes your argument less concise and less coherent.

9729.statement: Students do not embed their quotations.
9729.correction: If students don't embed their quotations, the response is not as concise as it could be. Being concise makes your response sophisticated.

9935.belief: Scrooge is selfish and miserable because he is a wicked person.
9935.statement: Students think that Scrooge is selfish and miserable because he is a wicked person.
9935.correction: Scrooge's miserliness comes from his deep-rooted fear of being poor.

9685.statement: Students believe that Dickens harshly condemns the wealthy.
9685.correction: Dickens only condemns people with money, who choose not to share it with those in need. This is exemplified in the character of Fezziwig.

9683.belief: Belle was never interested in having any money.
9683.statement: Students believe that Belle was never interested in having any money.
9683.correction: Belle was interested in having money - she just wanted to earn it with Scrooge over time.

9815.statement: Students tend to 'bolt' irrelevant context onto the end of analytical paragraphs.
9815.correction: Context should be integrated into students' responses and should enhance or support their arguments.

9907.belief: Once they have put their pen down and stopped writing, that they have finished.
9907.statement: Students think that once they have put their pen down and stopped writing, that they have finished.
9907.correction: Students should think of their first attempt as simply a first draft. The second redraft is their chance to fine tune their argument.

9688.belief: Father Christmas was always pictured wearing red.
9688.statement: Students believe that Father Christmas was always pictured wearing red.
9688.correction: Victorian depictions of Father Christmas show him wearing green, with a wreath of holly around his head.

9854.belief: Dickens' message about Christmas is focused solely on the importance of charity.
9854.statement: Students think that Dickens' message about Christmas is focused solely on the importance of charity.
9854.correction: Dickens uses the many Christmas scenes in this section of the novella to emphasise the importance of community and human connection.

9684.belief: Bob Cratchit represents the most poor group of people in society.
9684.statement: Students often believe that Bob Cratchit represents the most poor group of people in society.
9684.correction: Whilst Bob Cratchit certainly struggles for money and has to be resourceful to feed his family, he still has a job and a home.

7857.belief: Fred making fun of Scrooge is mean.
7857.statement: Pupils think that Fred making fun of Scrooge is mean.
7857.correction: Fred is shown to have a great sense of humour and this is what he's expressing when talking about his uncle. It is this sense of humour that enables him to remain optimistic despite financial struggle.

9817.statement: Students tend to struggle to understand how Scrooge has metaphorically fathered Ignorance and Want.
9817.correction: By being ignorant, Scrooge has neglected his social responsibility and nurtured inequality and injustice - the two children represent this.

9971.belief: The writer's method is just similes/metaphors etc.
9971.statement: Students think that the writer's method is just similes/metaphors etc.
9971.correction: The writer's method is anything that they do consciously - it's any conscious choice that they make.

9690.belief: The ghost shows Scrooge his future and that this will be Scrooge's fate.
9690.statement: Students believe that the ghost shows Scrooge his future and that this will be Scrooge's fate.
9690.correction: The ghost shows Scrooge the "shadows of things that may be". The word "may" is vital, as he suggests that it is never too late to change.

9686.belief: Dickens only offers a condemnation of the immorality exhibited by Mrs. Dilber.
9686.statement: Students believe that Dickens only offers a condemnation of the immorality exhibited by Mrs. Dilber.
9686.correction: Dickens, though he doesn't condone the character's behaviour, does empathise with her, and illustrates that she is the product of injustice.

7766.belief: Dickens is solely emphasising the value of human life.
7766.statement: Pupils think that Dickens is solely emphasising the value of human life.
7766.correction: Dickens is also emphasising the importance of what we do with our lives - how we use them to enrich other people's human experience.

9947.belief: That, in Stave 4, Scrooge is frightened of dying.
9947.statement: Students think that, in Stave 4, Scrooge is frightened of dying.
9947.correction: Scrooge is not frightened of death. He is frightened of dying without leaving a legacy because he has not contributed anything to society.

9733.statement: Students fail to recognise that Scrooge doesn't just buy the Cratchits any old turkey.
9733.correction: Scrooge buys the Cratchits the "prize" (or most expensive) turkey. This shows that he is truly generous, as he goes above and beyond.

9904.belief: The novella's title was chosen simply to reflect the festive period it covers.
9904.statement: Students think the novella's title was chosen simply to reflect the festive period it covers.
9904.correction: The title is more symbolic of Dickens' intentions - he intended for the message from this text to be spread far and wide, much like a carol.

9829.belief: Because this is an 'old book', it might not still bear a relevant message.
9829.statement: Students might think that because this is an 'old book', it might not still bear a relevant message.
9829.correction: The novella is a timeless classic because its message is universal. As long as there is injustice in the world, the text remains relevant.

9858.belief: It doesn't matter which quotations they select for use.
9858.statement: Students think that it doesn't matter which quotations they select for use.
9858.correction: It can be difficult to bring any new interpretations to commonly-used quotations, so try to pick some lesser-used ones.

9981.statement: Students do not understand that an argument should build in complexity.
9981.correction: Students should consider the structure of their argument. Which ideas need to come first in order to foreground other ideas?

1928.belief: Conflict only refers to physical conflict e.g. war.
1928.statement: Conflict only refers to physical conflict e.g. war
1928.correction: Conflict can be psychological, moral and between ideas, not just physical.

9000.belief: Romantic literature is about love and romance.
9000.statement: Romantic literature is about love and romance.
9000.correction: Romantic literature is concerned with human emotion but Romanticism was a movement that rejected the principles of the Enlightenment period.

3115.belief: The form of poem an author might choose means little to the message.
3115.statement: The form of poem an author might choose means little to the message
3115.correction: Poets pick their forms carefully, as we can see in 'Ozymandias' even the slight tweaking of form can impact the reading of the poem and its meaning.

6666.statement: Pupils might first read the poem as entirely literal. e.g. "black'ning church" refers to pollution of the industrial revolution.
6666.correction: Several ideas are metaphorical or symbolic in the poem. E.g. Blake refers to the corruption of the church (the church is also symbolic of religion as a whole).

9655.belief: The structure of the poem is entirely predictable.
9655.statement: The structure of the poem is entirely predictable.
9655.correction: Explain to pupils that Blake does break his rigid structure e.g. iambic tetrameter at times.

10354.belief: Topic sentences should compare language techniques, form and structure.
10354.statement: Topic sentences should compare language techniques, form and structure.
10354.correction: Topic sentences should focus on big ideas as it allows for meaningful comparison.

5626.belief: The poem depicts nothing more than a physical journey across a lake.
5626.statement: The poem depicts nothing more than a physical journey across a lake.
5626.correction: The poem's physical journey symbolises a spiritual journey and the ''growth'' of Wordsworth.

10595.belief: The use of the epic form is just to show Wordsworth's adventure.
10595.statement: The use of the epic form is just to show Wordsworth's adventure.
10595.correction: The use of epic form may suggest how nature is a heroic or legendary presence worthy of the epic poem form.

9003.belief: All Romantic poems from the anthology are equally comparable.
9003.statement: All Romantic poems from the anthology are equally comparable.
9003.correction: Some Romantic poems are more suitable for comparison, depending on which question you are asked.

1839.belief: A comparative response just needs to reference two poems.
1839.statement: A comparative response just needs to reference two poems.
1839.correction: A comparative response must explicitly compare two poems on big ideas. It is important to use discourse markers to signpost comparisons.

763.belief: Browning was writing about his own wife's domineering father.
763.statement: Browning was writing about his own wife's domineering father.
763.correction: Biographical moments in the poet's own life are not always relevant to the poem.

2527.belief: The Duke's presentation of himself is of absolute power.
2527.statement: The Duke's presentation of himself is of absolute power.
2527.correction: If you look deeper into Browning's presentation of the Duke, he is revealed to lack power.

2749.belief: Essay introductions should focus heavily on the poets and/or literary devices.
2749.statement: Essay introductions should focus heavily on the poets and/or literary devices.
2749.correction: Essay introductions should focus heavily on big ideas relevant to both poems and related to the question.

5636.belief: The poem merely documents a battle where many soldiers die.
5636.statement: The poem merely documents a battle where many soldiers die.
5636.correction: The poem addresses the issues of military error and blind obedience.

3668.belief: It is impressive to be able to identify and name structural techniques in an essay.
3668.statement: It is impressive to be able to identify and name structural techniques in an essay.
