3668.correction: It is much better to be able to comment on why certain structural techniques have been used and the effects of them, over just naming them in an essay.

5435.belief: People's attitudes to war are stagnant.
5435.statement: People's attitudes to war are stagnant.
5435.correction: Wilfred Owen's attitude towards war changed after he enlisted. His poetry explores this.

2866.belief: 'Exposure' only depicts the power of nature.
2866.statement: 'Exposure' only depicts the power of nature.
2866.correction: If we look critically, we can identify how Owen criticises and rejects powerful ideas and institutions, like other poets from the anthology.

5667.belief: Poetry about war is always based on first-hand experience.
5667.statement: Poetry about war is always based on first-hand experience.
5667.correction: Many poems about war are from the perspective of family members who are also impacted by their loved ones going to war.

9766.statement: Students may not initially see the natural imagery as relevant.
9766.correction: Explain to students that Ted Hughes was famous for his nature and animal poetry. He would have included these themes deliberately with a strong sense of purpose.

5284.belief: Outlining a similarity between two poems is sufficient to compare.
5284.statement: Outlining a similarity between two poems is sufficient to compare.
5284.correction: If you want to improve your work and ensure it is 'critical', you must interrogate the subtle differences between poems.

5137.belief: There is only one interpretation of the poem 'Storm on the Island'.
5137.statement: There is only one interpretation of the poem 'Storm on the Island'.
5137.correction: The poem can be a reflection of the power of nature, conflict between humans and nature, the political conflict or all.

9998.belief: All stylistic choices in a poem have to be in harmony with each other.
9998.statement: All stylistic choices in a poem have to be in harmony with each other.
9998.correction: Heaney's stylistic choices often seem to contradict each other but this could be symbolic of the conflict occurring between man and nature.

10915.belief: War links to conflict solely due to the violence and brutality between opposing sides whilst fighting.
10915.statement: War links to conflict solely due to the violence and brutality between opposing sides whilst fighting.
10915.correction: War can also link to mental conflict long after the fighting is done as we see in Armitage's poem.

9765.statement: Students may not initially notice the structural choices within the poem such as tense and enjambment.
9765.correction: Explain how language, structure, perspective and tense are always constructed meaningfully by the poet to match their purpose.

5653.belief: Most poems are deeply personal or emotional and are written spontaneously from the heart.
5653.statement: Most poems are deeply personal or emotional and are written spontaneously from the heart.
5653.correction: Armitage suggests that writing poetry about traumatic events can be a methodical process. He states that keeping some emotional distance can be helpful.

9666.statement: Students may associate war poetry with soldiers of the first world war and not consider other perspectives.
9666.correction: Many other people were affected by war in less obvious ways than the soldiers themselves.

7042.statement: Pupils may not notice the significance of the textile imagery.
7042.correction: The textile imagery was carefully chosen for the poem, Jane Weir would have been very conscious of putting this in as she was a textile designer.

8492.statement: Pupils may not understand the concept of photo developing when initially reading the poem and thus not realise what the poem is about.
8492.correction: Explain the process of photo developing film photographs in a dark room - the dark room is because photographs are light-sensitive.

9996.statement: Students may zoom into the suffering within the photos and not realise the complex emotions in the photographer himself.
9996.correction: Duffy, having seen her friends do the job of photojournalism, may have been privy to the complex and difficult emotions involved in this job. This could be why she focuses on the quiet trauma within the photographer.

10341.belief: The title of the poem 'Poppies' may cause the students to immediately link 'Poppies' with another WW1 poem e.g. 'Exposure'.
10341.statement: The title of the poem 'Poppies' may cause the students to immediately link 'Poppies' with another WW1 poem e.g. 'Exposure'.
10341.correction: It is better to look at comparing poems on the basis of themes and big ideas rather than the time periods in which they were based. 'Poppies' is not a WW1 poem but instead uses the symbol of a poppy in the title to explore grief and loss.

9789.statement: Students may not recognise the act of storytelling in the poem nor the four generations that feature.
9789.correction: Explain to the students the poem has one narrator but she is telling the story in 3rd person at the beginning, later revealing herself as the main character as the poem uses italics.

9794.statement: Students may not recognise the use of different perspectives in the poem to represent distance.
9794.correction: Explain to pupils that the dual narrative is a stylistic choice of Garland to show the mother telling the story to her own children as if she is not a part of it. She then slowly reveals the pilot is her own father.

9962.belief: All war poems are equally suitable for comparison.
9962.statement: Students may think that all war poems are equally suitable for comparison.
9962.correction: Grouping the war poems into distinct categories can help students see the subtle differences between poems that seem to be largely about the same thing.

5276.belief: Our personal response to a poem isn't a valid form of analysis.
5276.statement: Our personal response to a poem isn't a valid form of analysis.
5276.correction: Poems are outpourings of emotion and therefore our personal response is incredibly important as it allows us to work towards understanding the emotion behind the poem.

11196.belief: Your first reading of a poem should involve finding the techniques used.
11196.statement: That your first reading of a poem should involve finding the techniques used.
11196.correction: Reading the poem aloud and then considering the key images within the poem is a more effective way to consider the ideas in the poem.

252.belief: Analysing a poem's structure is boring and intimidating.
252.statement: That analysing a poem's structure is boring and intimidating.
252.correction: One way of looking at structure might be to imagine it as a heartbeat - why does the poem 'beat' regularly or irregularly? What emotion might that signify?

2019.belief: Context has to be a specific historical event or fact.
2019.statement: Context has to be a specific historical event or fact.
2019.correction: Considering the themes in the poet's other work is a valuable consideration of context.

5236.belief: The order of the poem doesn't matter.
5236.statement: That the order of the poem doesn't matter.
5236.correction: The order of the poem impacts when we are exposed to different ideas and emotions which influences the overall tone and meaning of the poem.

4517.belief: The meaning of a poem remains static throughout.
4517.statement: That the meaning of a poem remains static throughout.
4517.correction: In 'Homing', the subject's accent is portrayed as something negative at the beginning of the poem. However, by the end it is portrayed as something vital to identity and heritage.

9920.belief: Poets always try to make their poems sound pleasing.
9920.statement: Students sometimes think that poets always try to make their poems sound pleasing.
9920.correction: Poets may use harsh or disagreeable sounds within their poetry in order to emphasise meaning.

10909.belief: You only want to focus on differences in comparisons.
10909.statement: That you only want to focus on differences in comparisons.
10909.correction: When comparing poems, you want to begin by showing their overarching similarity and then explore the subtle differences.

9007.belief: Romantic poets were purely concerned with nature.
9007.statement: That Romantic poets were purely concerned with nature.
9007.correction: While nature is a prominent theme of many Romantic poems, Romantics were also social revolutionaries who criticised institutions such as the monarchy and the Church.

2695.belief: Enjambment simply creates flow in a poem.
2695.statement: That enjambment simply creates flow in a poem.
2695.correction: Enjambment usually links to the conceptual continuation of an idea of theme within the poem.

8960.belief: The right to education is the same all around the world.
8960.statement: The right to education is the same all around the world.
8960.correction: There are many places in the world where girls specifically have to fight for the right to education.

4836.belief: Natural imagery always links to the relationship between humanity and the environment.
4836.statement: That natural imagery always links to the relationship between humanity and the environment.
4836.correction: Natural imagery can also be used to show that a concept or idea is natural or that it is flourishing.

5489.belief: Philosophical ideas of time have no bearing on literature.
5489.statement: That philosophical ideas of time have no bearing on literature.
5489.correction: Considering the nature of time impacts the human experience and therefore has a bearing on literature since it explores what it means to be human.

2839.belief: Evoking ideas of deities always means that something is positive and divine.
2839.statement: Evoking ideas of deities always means that something is positive and divine.
2839.correction: While evoking deities can confer notions of divinity, we also need to consider the story behind the deity and how that story can add meaning to the narrative.

10031.belief: Subverting a poetic form means you are being critical of it.
10031.statement: Subverting a poetic form means you are being critical of it.
10031.correction: Subverting a poetic form means that you are in some way commenting on either the context of the form or the general theme of the form and using that to enhance the meaning of the poem.

3925.belief: A journey is always a physical undertaking.
3925.statement: That a journey is always a physical undertaking.
3925.correction: While many journeys are physical undertakings, you can also take a personal or spiritual journey towards improvement and growth.

10589.belief: The use of contrast in a poem is always intended to show friction and tension.
10589.statement: That the use of contrast in a poem is always intended to show friction and tension.
10589.correction: While the use of contrast shows difference, it doesn't necessarily have to show friction; instead, it might represent how we can coexist even though we are different.

5656.belief: Poems are purely works of imagination.
5656.statement: Poems are purely works of imagination.
5656.correction: While poems draw on the poet's imagination, many poems are drawn from real-life experiences which is why there is such an emotional resonance in them.

5240.belief: The order of words in a poem is random and unimportant.
5240.statement: That the order of words in a poem is random and unimportant.
5240.correction: The order of words creates a journey and progression through the poem which can influence the overall message.

2006.belief: The content of the poem matters more than who is speaking in the poem.
2006.statement: The content of the poem matters more than who is speaking in the poem.
2006.correction: The voice we hear in a poem is incredibly important for the meaning as it could show us who the poet deems as important or perhaps they are making a comment on who has agency in society.

5638.belief: A poem must have one singular tone.
5638.statement: That a poem must have one singular tone.
5638.correction: Often poems express complex emotions. For example, the speaker of 'Lines Written in Early Spring' feels both peace and disquiet at the same time.

10015.belief: The 'sublime' refers to something solely positive.
10015.statement: The 'sublime' refers to something solely positive.
10015.correction: While the 'sublime' suggests a reverence and awe for something, it also implies ideas of feeling insignificant and overwhelmed by it which therefore adds the idea of terror or fear.

2022.belief: Contextual information all has the same relevance and value.
2022.statement: That contextual information all has the same relevance and value.
2022.correction: When considering contextual information, you want to consider which information is the most relevant to helping us understand the meaning of the poem.

917.belief: A change in the rhyming pattern is unimportant to the meaning of the poem.
917.statement: A change in the rhyming pattern is unimportant to the meaning of the poem.
917.correction: A change in the rhyme could signify a change in emotion or a conflict/resolution has occurred.

1855.belief: Comparison answers should only focus on the differences between poems.
1855.statement: Comparison answers should only focus on the differences between poems.
1855.correction: Comparisons should focus on both the similarities and differences between the poems to reveal the subtle unique intentions of the poets.

1987.belief: We should consider imagery at literal, face value.
1987.statement: That we should consider imagery at literal, face value.
1987.correction: While considering the literal meaning is good for our understanding, we want to move beyond that to consider what a quotation or image symbolises and what it is saying about the wider ideas in the poem.

5157.belief: There is one singular tone or emotion within a poem.
5157.statement: There is one singular tone or emotion within a poem.
5157.correction: Often poems express complex and multiple emotions at one time.

2797.belief: Everyone considers time to be linear: moving from past, to present, to the future.
2797.statement: That everyone considers time to be linear: moving from past, to present, to the future.
2797.correction: Many works of literature consider time to be cyclical and consider us to be repeating or echoing what has happened in the past.

9071.belief: We all have the same metaphysical understanding of time.
9071.statement: That we all have the same metaphysical understanding of time.
9071.correction: While some people consider time to be linear, Seneviratne arguably considers time to be cyclical.

3059.belief: You should focus entirely on similarities or differences when writing a comparative response.
3059.statement: That you should focus entirely on similarities or differences when writing a comparative response.
3059.correction: When writing a comparative response, you should consider the overarching similarities and then consider the subtle differences within the similarities to create a nuanced response.

11134.belief: You should always write about the poem you know best.
11134.statement: You should always write about the poem you know best.
11134.correction: You should write about the two poems that form the best complementary pairing for the question.

11135.belief: You should write about each poem separately.
11135.statement: That you should write about each poem separately.
11135.correction: While writing about one poem at a time is one way to approach a comparison, it's usually more effective to weave your comparisons of the poems through the whole answer.

3123.belief: Form and structure are the same thing.
3123.statement: Form and structure are the same thing.
3123.correction: Form deals with the 'poetic rules' that govern a poem and helps us to categorise it along with other similar poems whereas structure deals with how the ideas in the poem are ordered and organised.

9253.belief: Sheers tells us that the couple have been arguing before heading out for their walk.
9253.statement: Sheers tells us that the couple have been arguing before heading out for their walk.
9253.correction: Sheers doesn't explicitly tell us that the couple have been arguing but subtly implies this using personification and pathetic fallacy in the first two stanzas. He describes how the couple are "silent and apart" to show their fragmented relationship.

5642.belief: The poem is set by a pond where a couple are walking.
5642.statement: The poem is set by a pond where a couple are walking.
5642.correction: The poem is set in the present day (for the speaker) and the speaker is looking back on the memory of walking around a pond with their ex-partner.

4868.belief: You need to include a reference to the wider context in every analytical paragraph.
4868.statement: You need to include a reference to the wider context in every analytical paragraph.
4868.correction: The best analytical responses only include relevant pieces of context and weave it subtly throughout. It is important to include context in your answer but it isn't necessary to include it in every paragraph.

73.belief: This is an account of Byron's affair with Lady Frances Webster.
73.statement: This is an account of Byron's affair with Lady Frances Webster.
73.correction: It is believed that is poem is inspired by Byron's affair with Lady Webster. It is not a factual account, only perhaps a creative interpretation of his feelings about this and other affairs he was known to have had.

4216.belief: The lines, "They know not I knew thee, / Who knew thee too well" refer to the close emotional relationship the couple had since they knew everything about each other.
4216.statement: The lines, "They know not I knew thee, / Who knew thee too well" refer to the close emotional relationship the couple had since they knew everything about each other.
4216.correction: These lines can also be read as a euphemism for the couple's sexual relationship, since 'know' was a term often used in the Bible to refer to sexual intercourse.

10309.belief: All three poems convey a negative view of romantic relationships.
10309.statement: All three poems convey a negative view of romantic relationships.
10309.correction: All three poems begin by conveying a negative view of romantic relationships. This continues throughout 'Neutral Tones' and 'When We Two Parted' however 'Winter Swans' undergoes a shift to a hopeful tone by the end as the couple are unified.

266.belief: Analytical paragraphs should be led by identification of writer's methods.
266.statement: Analytical paragraphs should be led by identification of writer's methods.
266.correction: An effective analytical response avoids 'feature-spotting'. Paragraphs should be led with a comparison of key ideas in each poem, followed by a detailed analysis of how the writers use methods to convey these ideas.

5645.belief: In this poem, the speaker mourns for their lover after they have died.
5645.statement: In this poem, the speaker mourns for their lover after they have died.
5645.correction: This could be a valid interpretation but there is no evidence to suggest the lover is definitely dead. In fact, the volta in L.9 has the speaker demand he return which implies that there is a chance they could be reunited with one another.

2873.belief: The extended metaphor of trees and vines represent her absent lover.
2873.statement: The extended metaphor of trees and vines represent her absent lover.
2873.correction: The extended metaphor of a tree symbolises her absent lover whereas the extended metaphor of the vines symbolises her fantastical thoughts of her lover while he is away from her.

9256.belief: Shelley was a Romantic poet which meant all of his poems were love poems.
9256.statement: Shelley was a Romantic poet which meant all of his poems were love poems.
9256.correction: Romantic poetry did sometimes focus on themes associated with love, but not exclusively. Romantic poetry is instead characterised by its dramatic approach to exploring abstract and emotional concepts such as a love, nature or the supernatural.

5641.belief: This poem is only about a Romantic view of love (from an abstract, philosophical perspective).
5641.statement: This poem is only about a Romantic view of love (from an abstract, philosophical perspective).
5641.correction: This poem appears to have an ulterior motive. Shelley uses language, form and structure to subtly persuade the listener to enter into a romantic relationship with him.

5634.belief: The poem is about a long-distance romantic relationship.
5634.statement: The poem is about a long-distance romantic relationship.
5634.correction: The relationship between the speaker and the man who sends her letters is ambiguous; it could be platonic, romantic or familial.

9536.belief: The speaker of the poem has unrequited romantic feelings for the man and yearns to be with him.
9536.statement: The speaker of the poem has unrequited romantic feelings for the man and yearns to be with him.
9536.correction: This is only one interpretation of the poem. Alternatively, the reference to "romance" in L.5 could imply that the speaker romanticises the natural world that she is so distanced from in her urban landscape and yearns to return to nature.

9257.belief: Shelley's poem presents a purely positive view of love.
9257.statement: Shelley's poem presents a purely positive view of love.
9257.correction: Interspersed among his speaker's overblown philosophical descriptions focused around the beauty of natural symmetry, it's possible to read an element of frustration that the speaker's feelings of desire are unrequited.

259.belief: Analysis should be led by identification of the writer's methods.
259.statement: Analysis should be led by identification of the writer's methods.
259.correction: Effective comparative analysis should be led by key ideas and then supported by textual evidence and identification of the writer's methods and intentions.

2584.belief: Eden Rock is a real place.
2584.statement: Eden Rock is a real place.
2584.correction: Eden Rock is a fictional place, devised by the poet Charles Causley. Causley confirms this but does suggest that he based the location on the Cornish landscape where he grew up.

2200.belief: You should decide on one main interpretation of text and focus on that in your analytical writing.
2200.statement: You should decide on one main interpretation of text and focus on that in your analytical writing.
2200.correction: Effective analytical writing often includes multiple interpretations of a text and careful consideration of the wider context.

9526.belief: The speaker is actually climbing a mountain.
9526.statement: The speaker is actually climbing a mountain.
9526.correction: The speaker compares the experience of climbing up his Grandfather's body as a child to climbing up a mountain.

234.belief: Ambivalence means you do not care either way (similar to indifference).
234.statement: Ambivalence means you do not care either way (similar to indifference).
234.correction: Ambivalence is when someone has mixed or conflicting feelings about something or someone.

9529.belief: The speaker explains how having children ruined her mother's life.
9529.statement: The speaker explains how having children ruined her mother's life.
9529.correction: While Duffy does explore how motherhood has contributed to her mother's loss of confidence and freedom, the final stanza of the poem shows them both having fun together so it is evident that there are many positive aspects to motherhood as well.

4724.belief: The mother feels a loss of her her beauty, confidence and independence after having a child.
4724.statement: The mother feels a loss of her her beauty, confidence and independence after having a child.
4724.correction: It's important to remember that the 'voice' we hear this from is the speaker's (the daughter). In this way, the negative connotations associated with motherhood could be interpreted as the speaker's guilt for taking her mother's freedom.

10311.belief: All three poems reflect on memories of a loved one who is now dead.
10311.statement: All three poems reflect on memories of a loved one who is now dead.
10311.correction: Causley's use of an uncanny setting implies that the two parents are now in the afterlife, guiding the speaker's "[c]rossing", however Duffy and Waterhouse use language linked to death/loss ("ghost", "pulse") but do not imply the relative has died.

261.belief: Every analysis paragraph should link to the wider context.
261.statement: Every analysis paragraph should link to the wider context.
261.correction: Effective analysis links to context only when relevant to the discussion of key ideas/methods and avoids 'bolt-on' sentences.

5647.belief: This poem is written in the form of a sonnet: it has 14 lines and a regular rhyme scheme.
5647.statement: This poem is written in the form of a sonnet: it has 14 lines and a regular rhyme scheme.
5647.correction: This poem does not strictly follow the sonnet form but does use many of its conventions. It contains 15, not 14 lines and doesn't use a regular rhyme scheme. It does however end with a rhyming couplet and uses iambic pentameter in places.

9533.belief: The speaker mourns the growing distance between him and his mother.
9533.statement: The speaker mourns the growing distance between him and his mother.
9533.correction: This is just one interpretation of the text; we could also infer that the speaker has felt stifled by their mother's involvement in their life until now and yearns for their independence.

5661.belief: A poet will always make choices with a clear intention or meaning.
5661.statement: A poet will always make choices with a clear intention or meaning.
5661.correction: Armitage reveals that poetic choices can be deliberately ambiguous, allowing for multiple interpretations and personal responses.

8094.belief: The parent and child never spoke or saw each other again after this moment in the poem.
8094.statement: Some pupils may think the parent and child never spoke or saw each other again after this moment in the poem.
8094.correction: The separation described in the poem isn't just physical but rather emotional. Day-Lewis describes a moment where the speaker feels like they lost a part of their son because he had grown up and gained his independence.

262.belief: Analysis paragraphs should lead by 'feature-spotting' a technique and then linking it to key ideas.
262.statement: Analysis paragraphs should lead by 'feature-spotting' a technique and then linking it to key ideas.
262.correction: The most effective analysis paragraphs lead with key ideas supported by evidence from the text, analysis of writer's methods, a justification of ideas and a link to the writer's intentions.

5621.belief: This poem is an autobiographical account of one of Heaney's childhood memories.
5621.statement: This poem is an autobiographical account of one of Heaney's childhood memories.
5621.correction: This collection, 'Death of Naturalist', is semi-autobiographical since it reflects on aspects of Heaney's childhood, growing up in a rural Irish farming community, but the poet has never confirmed that this particular memory is from his childhood.

9883.belief: In the last two lines of the poem, the father now follows behind the son while he is out ploughing a field.
9883.statement: Students may think that in the last two lines of the poem, the father now follows behind the son while he is out ploughing a field.
9883.correction: Although their roles have reversed, there is no indication that the last two lines involve the father and son ploughing. The echoes in the language merely symbolise that their roles have reversed as the son has grown up.

4723.belief: In 'Mother, any distance', the 'child' figure yearns for independence while the parent isn't ready to let them go.
4723.statement: In 'Mother, any distance', the 'child' figure yearns for independence while the parent isn't ready to let them go.
4723.correction: It is possible to interpret the poem in this way but it is also possible to infer that the speaker feels nervous about the prospect of their independence, worrying whether they will succeed or "fall".

3893.belief: It's important to include a contextual link in every analytical paragraph.
3893.statement: It's important to include a contextual link in every analytical paragraph.
3893.correction: Although it is important to include links to wider context in your overall response, it isn't necessary to include a contextual link in every analytical paragraph. In fact, 'bolt-on' contextual links should be avoided.

4503.belief: Mayhew describes everything in the prison in a negative light.
4503.statement: That Mayhew describes everything in the prison in a negative light.
4503.correction: Focus on the descriptions of the prisoners. Why does Mayhew present them in this way? What is he trying to say about prisoners?

3775.belief: Inference and analysis are the same thing.
3775.statement: Inference and analysis are the same thing.
3775.correction: Inference is about reading between the lines. Analysis focuses on unpicking writer's methods and explores their effects.

11156.belief: Writing down any number in a piece of non-fiction writing is enough to show you know how to use statistics.
11156.statement: Writing down any number in a piece of non-fiction writing is enough to show you know how to use statistics.
11156.correction: Statistics need to be credible. When creating your own statistics, you need to think carefully about how to make them sound believable by giving details like their source, date and data sample size.

5862.belief: The pronoun "you" is the only example of direct address.
5862.statement: The pronoun "you" is the only example of direct address.
5862.correction: Direct address is any way in which a writer directly addresses their audience. This could be a title, name or term.

5480.belief: Perspectives are simply positive or negative.
5480.statement: That perspectives are simply positive or negative.
5480.correction: Positive and negative can be useful words to initially consider a perspective, but then you must become more nuanced and use specific adjectives to identify feelings and perspectives.

10598.belief: You can only use figurative language in fictional writing.
10598.statement: You can only use figurative language in fictional writing.
10598.correction: Non-fiction writers, just like fiction writers, are trying to create interesting, original and compelling ideas that their readers will remember, enjoy and learn from.

11151.belief: When writing an extended piece of fiction or non-fiction, you should include every single method you know.
11151.statement: When writing an extended piece of fiction or non-fiction, you should include every single method you know.
11151.correction: Different texts are read for different reasons and by different audiences. It is your job, as the writer, to consider which are the best methods for your particular text. Just because you know how to use a method, doesn't mean you have to include it.

5527.belief: Placing ambiguous, short questions with direct address at the end of sentences is an effective rhetorical question. For example: Do you?/Don't you agree?
5527.statement: Placing ambiguous, short questions with direct address at the end of sentences is an effective rhetorical question. For example: Do you?/Don't you agree?
5527.correction: Think about the purpose of a rhetorical question and why we use them. Is this the best way to challenge and provoke thought or get a reaction from your audience?

1648.belief: Choosing vocabulary and ideas is the most important part of the writing process.
1648.statement: Choosing vocabulary and ideas is the most important part of the writing process.
1648.correction: Structural features can really elevate your writing, making it more cohesive and impactful so that your reader doesn't lose interest.

4022.belief: The language and structure of an informative website is always unexciting and dull.
4022.statement: The language and structure of an informative website is always unexciting and dull.
4022.correction: What is the best way to remember information? Are you more likely to remember if it is presented in an interesting and engaging way? Informative websites still need to engage their audience.

10969.belief: Websites don't need to be engaging if they only provide information.
10969.statement: Websites don't need to be engaging if they only provide information.
10969.correction: What is the purpose of a website? If you want people to read the information, how are you going to engage your reader?

8768.belief: When we read something for the first time, we are able to take in all of the important information.
8768.statement: When we read something for the first time, we are able to take in all of the important information.
8768.correction: We may need to read something over and over again to fully comprehend it. Using active reading strategies can also help us to fully engage with a new text.

8922.belief: A response is successful if it includes relevant quotes.
8922.statement: A response is successful if it includes relevant quotes.
8922.correction: We should aim high in our language analysis. That means going a step further to use the most meaningful evidence as well as looking for patterns in the text that help us gather a collection of evidence.

9773.statement: Students may misinterpret Murakami's semantic field and assume the text is a horror, mystery or thriller story.
9773.correction: If you really break down Murakami's use of semantic field, his word choice is more centered around dynamism of a living organism.

9710.statement: Students may confuse language and structural features.
9710.correction: Getting into a habit of asking a range of questions interrogating perspective, repetition, beginnings and endings can help students ease into the analysis of structure.

9741.statement: Students may find it difficult to harmonise their perspective choice with appropriate metaphors.
9741.correction: Spend time discussing less effective pairings e.g. a tree would would not perceive people in a city as 'ants' but an airplane might.

9671.belief: They need to identify and name specific structural devices in their structural analysis.
9671.statement: Students may assume that they need to identify and name specific structural devices in their structural analysis.
9671.correction: An answer simply referencing 'the beginning, middle and end' can make for a successful structural analysis.

10369.belief: The traditional story arc can only be applied to full narratives.
10369.statement: The traditional story arc can only be applied to full narratives.
10369.correction: You can find elements of the traditional story arc in writing of any length.

4224.belief: Lists cannot add sophistication to your writing.
4224.statement: Lists cannot add sophistication to your writing.
4224.correction: Varying the way we write lists can make our writing more sophisticated.

4857.belief: We need to describe sounds in a scene merely to tick off the fact we have used sensory language.
4857.statement: We need to describe sounds in a scene merely to tick off the fact we have used sensory language.
4857.correction: Thinking of scenarios where sound is particularly important can help us to use sound imagery more effectively.

2801.belief: 'Everyone is entitled to their own opinion', therefore there is no need to justify our opinions.
2801.statement: 'Everyone is entitled to their own opinion', therefore there is no need to justify our opinions.
2801.correction: Although we are all entitled to our opinion, justifying your opinion allows people to trust and listen to your opinion more carefully.

9965.belief: They only way to evaluate is to write whether they 'agree' or 'disagree' with something.
9965.statement: Students may think that they only way to evaluate is to write whether they 'agree' or 'disagree' with something.
9965.correction: In Learning Cycle 2, students learn that they can phrase and signpost their evaluations in a more sophisticated way, directly commenting on the writer's craft with evaluative adverbs.

9717.statement: Students may be confused about when the extract is taking place or what war the extract is about as it references multiple moments of time.
9717.correction: The novel opening takes place during the siege of Sarajevo in the 1990s. However, the reference to the aftermath of WW2 is significant in universalising the themes and messages of the novel.

4409.belief: We can only manipulate time in one way in a narrative.
4409.statement: We can only manipulate time in one way in a narrative.
4409.correction: When we know the effect that we want our flashbacks and flashforwards to have, we can use both.

9851.belief: Being critical means to talk about the negative aspects of something.
9851.statement: Students may think that being critical means to talk about the negative aspects of something.
9851.correction: We can be critical by judging something positively or negatively.

8571.statement: Pupils may use objects to symbolise ideas but the object may not quite match the idea e.g. violence represented by a flower.
8571.correction: Thinking about the feelings that an object makes us feel might help us to decide whether it will be an appropriate symbolic object.

5544.belief: Planning each paragraph to describe a different aspect of the scene will always create an engaging description.
5544.statement: Planning each paragraph to describe a different aspect of the scene will always create an engaging description.
5544.correction: Describing something different in each paragraph does not necessarily lead to an interesting description - it is the way in which the paragraphs link and build curiosity and tension that can make it more engaging.

5877.belief: Proofreading your work is not important if you plan it.
5877.statement: Proofreading your work is not important if you plan it.
5877.correction: Proofreading is equally important as planning. In pressured writing environments, we can easily make mistakes that we are not aware of.

9866.belief: Sometimes students think that a focused summary requires analysis of language.
9866.statement: Sometimes students think that a focused summary requires analysis of language.
9866.correction: Analysis requires you to zoom in and comment in detail about language choices. Why might this not be useful for a summary, where the aim is to be succinct and give a brief overview of a text?

9564.belief: Spotting lots of different features makes a good analysis.
9564.statement: That spotting lots of different features makes a good analysis.
9564.correction: Simply spotting a feature is too superficial. The best analysis will say a lot about little. Being able to develop multiple comments on a single feature, creates a much better more in-depth analysis.

4293.belief: Looking at other essays is cheating or copying.
4293.statement: Looking at other essays is cheating or copying.
4293.correction: Working with model responses helps develop your critical skills in order to evaluate your own work. Using and adapting others' ideas is a great thing to do!

8939.belief: Rhetorical devices always have the same effect.
8939.statement: Rhetorical devices always have the same effect.
8939.correction: Although we can make some assumptions about the effect of devices, considering specific information like the writer's intention and form will give a much more detailed and nuanced explanation.

5481.belief: Persuasive, issue based speeches have to maintain a serious tone.
5481.statement: Persuasive, issue based speeches have to maintain a serious tone.
5481.correction: Look at Malala's use of humour and anecdote. By engaging the audience in this way she holds their attention enough to make them listen to the serious messages.

10136.belief: Talking about why you like something is a good topic for a speech.
10136.statement: Talking about why you like something is a good topic for a speech.
10136.correction: Although it is important to choose something that interests you, you need to ensure the topic that you choose will enable you to present some complex ideas and use sophisticated vocabulary.

2470.belief: You don't need to, or shouldn't, use rhetorical devices in your topic or concluding sentences.
2470.statement: You don't need to, or shouldn't, use rhetorical devices in your topic or concluding sentences.
2470.correction: Just because the topic sentences introduce the main idea for the paragraph, that does not mean the topic sentence can't be really creative and engaging. It's crucial that it is engaging to motivate the reader to learn more about the topic.

5427.statement: Some people might think that letter writing has no place in modern society.
5427.correction: While other forms of communication have overtaken letter writing in popularity, letter writing is still necessary for many professional purposes.

2008.belief: It is the content of your argument that makes it persuasive rather than the construction.
2008.statement: It is the content of your argument that makes it persuasive rather than the construction.
2008.correction: The way you construct your argument directly impacts how persuasive it is to the reader.

10628.belief: Any use of personification will be effective in your writing.
10628.statement: Any use of personification will be effective in your writing.
10628.correction: In order to be effective, personification has to evoke a response that will make the reader feel persuaded by your argument.

1980.belief: The connection between the subject and object of a sentence doesn't matter in persuasive writing.
1980.statement: That the connection between the subject and object of a sentence doesn't matter in persuasive writing.
1980.correction: Using active or passive voice can affect the tone of your writing and how the reader responds to it.

10668.belief: You should always use words with high modality (must, need, have to) to make your writing seem persuasive.
10668.statement: That you should always use words with high modality (must, need, have to) to make your writing seem persuasive.
10668.correction: Exclusively using words with high modality can make your tone seem too direct and, therefore, make the reader feel defensive.

2391.belief: You should be very direct, almost aggressive in your persuasive writing.
2391.statement: That you should be very direct, almost aggressive in your persuasive writing.
2391.correction: While directness can convey confidence, an overly direct tone can be off-putting for the recipient and cause them to become defensive.

4355.belief: Main and subordinate clauses are merely grammatical terms not worthy of analysis.
4355.statement: Main and subordinate clauses are merely grammatical terms not worthy of analysis.
4355.correction: A writer's decision to use subordinate and main clauses is a creative choice. Their use can achieve different things (e.g. tension, pace).

10597.belief: You should use exclamative sentences all the way through your writing to show tension.
10597.statement: You should use exclamative sentences all the way through your writing to show tension.
10597.correction: It can be more effective to begin with declarative sentences and progress to exclamative sentences to show the rising tension.

5920.belief: Punctuation is only used to ensure writing makes sense.
5920.statement: Punctuation is only used to ensure writing makes sense.
5920.correction: Punctuation can be a stylistic choice from a writer, contributing to the tension of a story.

9664.statement: Students should aim to include as many punctuation types as possible.
9664.correction: The best writing uses punctuation sparingly to enhance the overall effect of the writing.

4279.belief: As long as the words are related in some way it is an effective semantic field.
4279.statement: As long as the words are related in some way it is an effective semantic field.
4279.correction: The best semantic fields vary their word types, including verbs, adjectives and nouns that are related in some way.

10739.belief: Using sophisticated vocabulary alone is enough to make my writing great.
10739.statement: Using sophisticated vocabulary alone is enough to make my writing great.
10739.correction: Although sophisticated vocabulary is good, there are lots of smaller strategies that can also make writing effective.

9195.belief: All sensory imagery is equally effective.
9195.statement: All sensory imagery is equally effective.
9195.correction: The best sensory imagery employs precise language to achieve specific atmospheres.

249.correction: The best analysis - with the richest commentary - will also spend time focusing on structural decisions a writer makes.

5874.belief: Proofreading entails reading through a piece of writing once to check for errors.
5874.statement: Proofreading entails reading through a piece of writing once to check for errors.
5874.correction: There are a variety of different strategies for proofreading (LC3). Encourage students to use the strategies that work best for them.

9185.correction: A semantic field based around an abstract noun (regret) is more sophisticated than one based around something simple (e.g. the rain).

2457.belief: You don't need to analyse non-fiction texts - just absorb the information.
2457.statement: That you don't need to analyse non-fiction texts - just absorb the information.
2457.correction: Analysing non-fiction texts is essential because it helps us understand who is offering us this information and why are they offering it to us.

8348.belief: Using long quotations offers the best evidence for your point.
8348.statement: Pupils sometimes think that using long quotations offers the best evidence for your point.
8348.correction: Using short, embedded quotations is the most effective way of evidencing your ideas.

2458.belief: We don't need to analyse the writer's attitude in non-fiction because it's all factual information.
2458.statement: We don't need to analyse the writer's attitude in non-fiction because it's all factual information.
2458.correction: Analysing the writer's attitude in non-fiction is important because it helps us to understand why the writer has presented information in a certain way and how they want us to interpret the information.

1837.belief: Comparative paragraphs should only focus on differences.
1837.statement: Comparative paragraphs should only focus on differences.
1837.correction: The most effective comparisons look for subtle differences within larger similarities.

9549.belief: A speech should be approached like any other written text.
9549.statement: A speech should be approached like any other written text.
9549.correction: Speeches should be approached in a very different way to other types of written text as they are designed to be spoken aloud. Long sentences, for example, should avoided since they are difficult for audiences to follow when heard aloud.

267.belief: Anaphora and refrain are the same. They are both types of repetition.
267.statement: Anaphora and refrain are the same. They are both types of repetition.
267.correction: While both anaphora and a refrain are both types of repetition, they function differently. Anaphora occurs when the beginning of a sentence is repeated, whereas a refrain when a key idea is repeated throughout a text, like a chorus in a song.

222.belief: Alliteration and onomatopoeia are devices used only in fiction writing (e.g. stories).
222.statement: Alliteration and onomatopoeia are devices used only in fiction writing (e.g. stories).
222.correction: Alliteration and onomatopoeia are both types of aural device because they link to how writers use sounds. This means they are particularly useful for speeches because they are delivered aloud (as opposed to read).

9186.belief: Semicolons can be used to join any two clauses of any length.
9186.statement: Semicolons can be used to join any two clauses of any length.
9186.correction: The clauses joined by a semicolon must be both be independent clauses (which means they make sense of their own) and should be linked in terms of their subject matter.

8941.belief: A rhetorical question is never answered. It is designed to make people think.
8941.statement: A rhetorical question is never answered. It is designed to make people think.
8941.correction: While a rhetorical question is designed to encourage the reader or audience to consider their views on the subject matter, a writer can choose to answer the rhetorical question conveying their opinions (but they don't have to).

4020.belief: Language devices - like extended analogies - are more appropriate for analysis in stories and narrative fiction.
4020.statement: Language devices - like extended analogies - are more appropriate for analysis in stories and narrative fiction.
4020.correction: Using language devices such as extended analogies can be a very effective way of communicating ideas in non-fiction writing.

2310.belief: We can develop a personal response by asking the same questions of every non-fiction text.
2310.statement: That we can develop a personal response by asking the same questions of every non-fiction text.
2310.correction: While some questions are universal, a non-fiction text such as a personal essay may require us to ask questions about what the writer want us to understand about their lives in order for us to respond to it.

2972.belief: Figurative language such as similes belongs in fictional writing rather than non-fiction.
2972.statement: Figurative language such as similes belongs in fictional writing rather than non-fiction.
2972.correction: Non-fiction writing is all about informing, persuading or educating the reader and therefore similes can be a very useful device to explain ideas to the reader.

11138.belief: A writer's attitude will remain the same throughout a non-fiction text.
11138.statement: A writer's attitude will remain the same throughout a non-fiction text.
11138.correction: If a writer is recounting an experience then their attitude may change from the beginning to the end of their text.

1842.belief: You can only compare methods that both writers use when comparing non-fiction texts.
1842.statement: You can only compare methods that both writers use when comparing non-fiction texts.
1842.correction: It can be very effective to compare why one writer might choose to use a certain method while another writer may choose not to use it.

3566.belief: Hyperbole and exaggeration are the same thing.
3566.statement: Hyperbole and exaggeration are the same thing.
3566.correction: Exaggeration is a broad term for overstating something beyond the truth, while hyperbole is a specific type of exaggeration used deliberately for emphasis or effect, often in a dramatic or humorous way.

2595.belief: Effective analysis writing explores the attitudes in the first text and then, in another paragraph, explores the attitudes in the second text.
2595.statement: Effective analysis writing explores the attitudes in the first text and then, in another paragraph, explores the attitudes in the second text.
2595.correction: The most effective comparative analysis writing will weave comparisons of both texts together. The response will ideally move between examples from each text, weighing up and evaluating the writer's choices in each.

8841.belief: Refuting counter-arguments is enough to create an impact.
8841.statement: Refuting counter-arguments is enough to create an impact.
8841.correction: Although it is good practice to refute counter-arguments, we can also use language devices when we do so to make them even more powerful.

1913.belief: In the conclusion of your speech, you should introduce one final point that helps to persuade any audience members who haven't been convinced throughout your speech.
1913.statement: In the conclusion of your speech, you should introduce one final point that helps to persuade any audience members who haven't been convinced throughout your speech.
1913.correction: Your conclusion isn't really the place to introduce new ideas as it will be tricky for you to fully develop them before you finish speaking. Instead, use the conclusion to summarise your key ideas and reinforce your central message.

5426.statement: Some people think that crime fiction is a trivial genre.
5426.correction: Crime fiction explores the dark side of human psychology and reading crime fiction where the crime is solved can help reassure us that society is a safe place and criminals are punished.

11136.belief: To write a reassuring resolution all you need to do is tie the narrative points together.
11136.statement: That to write a reassuring resolution all you need to do is tie the narrative points together.
11136.correction: To craft a reassuring resolution then you might think about how you can use imagery, symbolism and figurative language to convey calm emotions.

1703.belief: Cliffhangers are only designed to make the reader carry on reading.
1703.statement: That cliffhangers are only designed to make the reader carry on reading.
1703.correction: Cliffhangers can entice the reader to continue reading, but they can also create tension and subvert the reader's expectations.

335.belief: Anti-climaxes are always disappointing for the reader.
335.statement: Anti-climaxes are always disappointing for the reader.
335.correction: While unexpected, anti-climaxes are subjective and not necessarily always disappointing.

5603.belief: Plot twists typically reveal something hidden about a character.
5603.statement: Plot twists typically reveal something hidden about a character.
5603.correction: While plot twists may reveal something hidden about a character, plot twists can be used to subvert our expectations of life and resolution.

5602.belief: Plot twists always turn a happy story to an unhappy story.
5602.statement: That plot twists always turn a happy story to an unhappy story.
5602.correction: While some classic plot twists do turn a happy story to an unhappy story, it's not true of all plot twists.

2445.belief: It doesn't matter how you end a story - people will have the same emotional reaction.
2445.statement: It doesn't matter how you end a story - people will have the same emotional reaction.
2445.correction: The way that you end a story drastically impacts the lasting emotional impression and how a reader interprets the story.

5649.belief: All of the poems in this anthology focus on a particular war from history.
5649.statement: All of the poems in this anthology focus on a particular war from history.
5649.correction: There are some war poems in the anthology which focus on particular conflicts (e.g. 'Destruction of Sennacherib' and 'Charge of the Light Brigade') but others which focus more on societal conflicts (e.g. racism, social class).

11039.belief: The woman in the poem didn't love her baby because she abandoned them when the bomb went off.
11039.statement: The woman in the poem didn't love her baby because she abandoned them when the bomb went off.
11039.correction: It's difficult to hold someone to account for their actions in a traumatic event like this. Furthermore, the description of the "burden" the woman abandons could also be interpreted as an emotional burden that the shock causes her to leave behind.

5630.belief: This poem focuses on the moral complexities of war and conflict.
5630.statement: This poem focuses on the moral complexities of war and conflict.
5630.correction: This poem is less about war and more about the stories we tell/hear/see about it. Arguably, Satyamurti suggests that there is no way to fully capture traumatic experiences like this since neither the picture nor caption capture what really happened.

5650.belief: Both poems are based on a firsthand experience of war.
5650.statement: Both poems are based on a firsthand experience of war.
5650.correction: Only 'Exposure' is based on firsthand experience since Owen was serving as a WWI British soldier while writing. Satyamurti's poem wasn't based on any one particular person, event or conflict.

5648.belief: This poem is written about soldiers fighting in WWI.
5648.statement: This poem is written about soldiers fighting in WWI.
5648.correction: This poem was published during the Second Boer War (1899-1902) fought during the Victorian era. The First World War wouldn't begin for another 12 years.

2659.belief: The 'enemy' soldier was a similar person to the speaker - he did a similar job and was of a similar social status.
2659.statement: The 'enemy' soldier was a similar person to the speaker - he did a similar job and was of a similar social status.
2659.correction: We only learn about the 'enemy' soldier through the speaker's perspective. In stanza 4, the speaker infers what the man's life was like and, in turn, reveals a lot about his life and motivations for joining the army.

10869.belief: The Vietnam War was a conflict fought between the US and the country of Vietnam.
10869.statement: The Vietnam War was a conflict fought between the US and the country of Vietnam.
10869.correction: Following the First Indochina War, Vietnam was split into two regions: communist controlled North Vietnam and South Vietnam, controlled by a non-communist government (supported by the US). The Vietnam War was fought between these two regions.

5646.belief: This poem takes a retrospective view on the Vietnam War, looking back on the devastation many years later.
5646.statement: This poem takes a retrospective view on the Vietnam War, looking back on the devastation many years later.
5646.correction: The poem is set in an alternate future, set after the Vietnam War had ended (and the US had won). It was actually first published in 1968, while the conflict was still ongoing. The war didn't end until 1975.

4406.belief: 'The Man He Killed', 'Exposure', 'War Photographer' and 'What Were They Like?' display a purely negative and critical attitude to war.
4406.statement: 'The Man He Killed', 'Exposure', 'War Photographer' and 'What Were They Like?' display a purely negative and critical attitude to war.
4406.correction: Thomas Hardy's 'The Man He Killed' certainly questions the dehumanising nature of war but arguably isn't quite as critical as other war poems since in the last stanza the speaker describes war and killing enemy soldiers as "quaint" and "curious".

10445.belief: The Troubles was a war that occurred between the armies of the UK and the Republic of Ireland.
10445.statement: The Troubles was a war that occurred between the armies of the UK and the Republic of Ireland.
10445.correction: The Troubles were fought in Northern Ireland between the unionists (who wanted NI to remain in the UK) and the nationalists (who wanted NI to join the ROI). Most of the fighting occurred between paramilitary groups.

599.belief: 'Belfast Confetti' is a metaphor created by Carson in this poem.
599.statement: 'Belfast Confetti' is a metaphor created by Carson in this poem.
599.correction: The term 'Belfast Confetti' was used during The Troubles to refer to the homemade bombs used in the fighting. They were called this because they were filled with shrapnel which, when detonated, sprayed in the sky like confetti.

9006.belief: Romantic poetry is always about love.
9006.statement: Romantic poetry is always about love.
9006.correction: Romantic and romantic are two different words. The former, Romantic, refers to a cultural and artistic movement in the 1700-1800s whereas the latter, romantic, means 'linked to love and relationships'.

688.belief: Blake was a Romantic poet and artist and thus was critical of many societal beliefs and attitudes, namely religion which was called into question in the Enlightenment period just prior to this.
688.statement: Blake was a Romantic poet and artist and thus was critical of many societal beliefs and attitudes, namely religion which was called into question in the Enlightenment period just prior to this.
688.correction: The Romantics did acknowledge and agree with many Enlightenment ideas but, by and large, they were religious in their writing. Blake was a deeply religious man and his critique of religion was focused mainly on how it was interpreted by society.

9538.belief: The speaker's foe was poisoned by the fruit he grew.
9538.statement: The speaker's foe was poisoned by the fruit he grew.
9538.correction: At the beginning of the poem, the speaker seems to imply that the tree is metaphorical since it "grew" from the speaker's anger and resentment so perhaps the death of the "foe" could symbolise another sort of revenge undertaken by the speaker.

784.belief: Byron based this poem on a religious conflict which occurred during his lifetime.
784.statement: Byron based this poem on a religious conflict which occurred during his lifetime.
784.correction: This poem describes a conflict which was described in the Bible, when King Sennacherib and the Assyrian army attempted to attack Jerusalem and were prevented by a divine intervention.

785.belief: Byron portrays the Assyrians as evil predators because this was what he believed they were like.
785.statement: Byron portrays the Assyrians as evil predators because this was what he believed they were like.
785.correction: Arguably, we can't know Byron's feelings on this matter. It's more likely that he portrays the Assyrians in this way to emphasise the power of God when he is able to easily decimate such a formidable enemy.

1927.belief: Conflict always occurs between one person and at least one other person.
1927.statement: Conflict always occurs between one person and at least one other person.
1927.correction: Conflict can be within someone's own mind (inner conflict) and it doesn't always have to involve people at all. Powerful ideas or forces can be in conflict with one another too.

3436.belief: 'Half-caste' is a word used to describe people whose parents have different racial or cultural backgrounds.
3436.statement: 'Half-caste' is a word used to describe people whose parents have different racial or cultural backgrounds.
3436.correction: This is a historical term and is now considered inappropriate and disrespectful to use. Instead, we may use terms such as 'mixed race' or 'dual heritage' to discuss someone's cultural or racial background.

5643.belief: The poem is solely directed at the silent listener ("yu") who is addressed in the opening of the poem.
5643.statement: The poem is solely directed at the silent listener ("yu") who is addressed in the opening of the poem.
5643.correction: It could be argued that this silent listener could symbolise all readers (or listeners) of this poem since the speaker discusses how they will behave when they are "introduced" to the "yu" figure, implying they haven't yet met.

875.belief: Casey was working class and wrote about her own life experiences in the poem.
875.statement: Casey was working class and wrote about her own life experiences in the poem.
875.correction: Not much is known about Mary Casey. She did come from a working class background but we cannot be certain if this poem reflects her own life experiences. This is why it is important to use tentative language when analysing a literary text.

876.belief: Casey's playful tone makes light of class conflict.
876.statement: Casey's playful tone makes light of class conflict.
876.correction: While Casey uses a playful tone which does lighten the mood of the poem, her use of repeated rhetorical questions foregrounds her more serious message about class prejudice.

628.belief: Benjamin Zephaniah wrote in an exaggerated phonetic way to represent the accent of the speaker.
628.statement: Benjamin Zephaniah wrote in an exaggerated phonetic way to represent the accent of the speaker.
628.correction: Zephaniah was a dub poet which meant that he performed his work aloud. This phonetic spelling should be viewed more as a transcription of Zephaniah's own cultural patois.

11204.belief: Zephaniah's description of his "mother country" shows that his Jamaican cultural identity is more important to him that his British identity.
11204.statement: Zephaniah's description of his "mother country" shows that his Jamaican cultural identity is more important to him that his British identity.
11204.correction: Prior to Jamaican independence in 1962, many Jamaicans referred to the UK as their "mother country". This suggests that Zephaniah's British identity is very important to him.

2020.belief: Context should be used in every paragraph of a comparative analytical response.
2020.statement: Context should be used in every paragraph of a comparative analytical response.
2020.correction: While it is extremely important to use relevant contextual information to shape interpretations of the two poems being compared, it isn't necessary to include it in every paragraph unless it is relevant to the overall argument you are making.

244.belief: You should analyse one poem and then analyse the second, making your comparisons at this point.
244.statement: You should analyse one poem and then analyse the second, making your comparisons at this point.
244.correction: The best analysis writing weaves comparisons throughout. A great way to practise this is by beginning each paragraph with a topic sentence that uses correlative conjunctions (e.g. both... and...).

333.belief: An anthology only explores the title theme.
333.statement: That an anthology only explores the title theme.
333.correction: An anthology could also explore the inverse of the title theme in order to highlight particular ideas or concepts.

9295.belief: Simple poetry is not as good as complex poetry.
9295.statement: That simple poetry is not as good as complex poetry.
9295.correction: Arguably, good poetry creates an emotional response in the reader and evokes a particular image or impression.

4869.belief: You need to know the exact rhythm to analyse it.
4869.statement: That you need to know the exact rhythm to analyse it.
4869.correction: Determining whether a rhythm is regular or irregular can be a way of analysing the structure.

9005.belief: Romantic poems always present nature in a positive light.
9005.statement: That Romantic poems always present nature in a positive light.
9005.correction: Sometimes Romantic poets may show the devastation that humanity has caused nature or talk about nature in a grieving way.

9009.belief: The Romantics only wrote about nature.
9009.statement: That the Romantics only wrote about nature.
9009.correction: Often Romantic writers also wrote about a nostalgia for the past.

9393.belief: Society has always considered childhood as a space for play and exploration.
9393.statement: That society has always considered childhood as a space for play and exploration.
9393.correction: Before the Enlightenment, children were generally considered small versions of adults.

10168.correction: While we might associate 'temper' with a 'temper tantrum', 'temper' can refer to any emotional frame of mind.

10644.belief: The use of sibilance creates a harsh, sinister atmosphere.
10644.statement: That the use of sibilance creates a harsh, sinister atmosphere.
10644.correction: While the hissing sound of sibilance can create a harsh atmosphere, we can also interpret it as a shushing sound that creates a calm atmosphere.

10761.belief: Using your imagination to create imaginary games is a way of withdrawing from the world.
10761.statement: That using your imagination to create imaginary games is a way of withdrawing from the world.
10761.correction: While imaginary games can be used to withdraw from the world, our imaginations come from things we have seen or experienced and therefore imaginary games can be a way of connecting to the world and finding your place in it.

3604.belief: Idyllic settings stay the same forever.
3604.statement: That idyllic settings stay the same forever.
3604.correction: Arguably, Landon's 'Captain Cook (To My Brother)' suggests that an idyllic place does not last forever.

3603.correction: Idleness can also mean enjoying periods of rest and relaxation.

9275.belief: Sibilance is only used to create a sinister atmosphere.
9275.statement: Sibilance is only used to create a sinister atmosphere.
9275.correction: The repetition of 's' sound could also create a calming, soothing sound.

5662.belief: A poet can only be a part of one literary movement.
5662.statement: That a poet can only be a part of one literary movement.
5662.correction: Often, we can see poets as referencing more than one literary movement and that can help us understand the poem.

253.belief: Analysing punctuation isn't an effective way to approaching a poem.
253.statement: That analysing punctuation isn't an effective way to approaching a poem.
253.correction: Punctuation can affect a reader's journey through the poem as well as their emotional response.

10297.belief: Every poem in the anthology is equally suitable for every potential question.
10297.statement: Thinking that every poem in the anthology is equally suitable for every potential question.
10297.correction: While there are common links between the poems, some have more tenuous connections than others.

5652.belief: Poems always consider the speaker's individual feelings and emotions.
5652.statement: That poems always consider the speaker's individual feelings and emotions.
5652.correction: Poems often use the speaker as a way of observing life around them and commenting on wider society.

3116.belief: The form of a poem doesn't influence our analysis.
3116.statement: That the form of a poem doesn't influence our analysis.
3116.correction: The chosen form can influence our perception of the theme of a poem and give us a clue into the writer's intentions.

2504.statement: That dreams aren't based on reality.
2504.correction: Dreams often draw on our previous memories or experiences.

3622.belief: Imagery has one set meaning and connotations.
3622.statement: That imagery has one set meaning and connotations.
3622.correction: The connotations of an image can change depending on the language used in relation to it.

5273.belief: Our identities are a singular, unchanging thing.
5273.statement: That our identities are a singular, unchanging thing.
5273.correction: Our identifies are made up of many things that can change and evolve over time.

5115.belief: There is one accepted interpretation of a poem.
5115.statement: That there is one accepted interpretation of a poem.
5115.correction: People may interpret and respond to poetry differently because poetry is, at its core, about emotion and we all have different emotion responses to stimuli.

1853.belief: Comparing poems means focusing on their similarities.
1853.statement: That comparing poems means focusing on their similarities.
1853.correction: The most effective comparisons look for subtle differences within wider similarities.

8265.statement: Pupils may think that the speaker is Rumens herself.
8265.correction: Rumens herself did not experience the emigration that the poem describes. She may have written the poem based on her fascination with people and culture. She may have written the poem to appeal to all that have experienced a story of emigration.

6826.statement: Pupils may not initially link all of the examples of personification together.
6826.correction: Explain to pupils that finding patterns in the text can be very useful to help create a thoughtful idea about the poem.

3519.belief: A home is just a set of bricks and mortar.
3519.statement: That a home is just a set of bricks and mortar.
3519.correction: A home offers us a place of refuge and safety - without a home we feel lost and unsure.

4485.correction: While material possessions can be replaced, nevertheless they do provide a sense of safety and comfort for us.

2580.belief: An economic migrant and a refugee are the same thing.
2580.statement: That an economic migrant and a refugee are the same thing.
2580.correction: A refugee is someone who has been forced to leave their country in order to escape war, persecution or natural disaster.

8837.belief: Refugees come from places that have always been war torn and a disaster zone.
8837.statement: That refugees come from places that have always been war torn and a disaster zone.
8837.correction: Refugees can come from anywhere - places that used to be beautiful but have changed through war, regime change or natural disaster.

10501.belief: All types of negative feelings are the same.
10501.statement: That all types of negative feelings are the same.
10501.correction: There are nuances within negativity - some negative emotions might stem from fear, anger, jealousy or uncertainty.

9925.belief: There is a 'right' answer when it comes to poetry - that the poem has to have one meaning.
9925.statement: Students sometimes think there is a 'right' answer when it comes to poetry - that the poem has to have one meaning.
9925.correction: The beauty of poetry is that it means something different to everybody - there is no 'right' answer - there are a series of possible answers.

7676.belief: Brooke fought and died in the war because he wrote a war poem.
7676.statement: Pupils might think that Brooke fought and died in the war because he wrote a war poem.
7676.correction: Although Brooke bravely volunteered to fight in the war, he never actually engaged in any military action. Unfortunately, Brooke died from septicaemia on a ship en route to battle.

9836.belief: Brooke fought and died in the war because he wrote a war poem.
9836.statement: Students might think that Brooke fought and died in the war because he wrote a war poem.
9836.correction: Although Brooke bravely volunteered to fight in the war, he never actually engaged in any military action. Unfortunately, Brooke died from septicaemia on a ship en route to battle.

9769.statement: Students often make the mistake of thinking that, like many of the other war poems, this poem was written by a soldier at the time of the war.
9769.correction: This poem is not a personal account; Sheers wrote this poem in 2005. He wanted to raise awareness about the loss of Welsh lives in Mametz Wood and illustrate how destructive war is.

9732.statement: Students fail to recognise that the poem itself is a kind of memorial for the 38th division in the Battle of Mametz Wood.
9732.correction: The poem immortalises the Welsh soldiers in the 38th division, who lay undiscovered for decades, their stories untold. In this sense, the poem itself has become these soldiers' legacy.

9730.statement: Students often fail to appreciate the significance of the speaker being the soldier's wife.
9730.correction: The perspective the poem is written from is deeply significant. Perhaps Armitage chose to write the poem from the perspective of the wife because the soldier is too traumatised to speak of his own experiences.

9861.belief: The entire poem is in rhyming couplets.
9861.statement: Students think that the entire poem is in rhyming couplets.
9861.correction: Only the beginning of the poem is written in rhyming couplets. The couplets fade to pararhymes and then to non-rhyming couplets by the end of the poem, possibly to reflect the soldier's pain fading and the healing process.

8377.statement: Pupils often think that the wife receives two letters.
8377.correction: The wife receives a telegram and a letter. Both the irony and the tragedy are in the fact that, due to the quick nature of telegrams, the wife receives news of her husband's death before she receives his letter.

9784.statement: Students are quick to identify a poem's rhyme scheme, but they often fail to explain its effect or why it has been used.
9784.correction: In this poem, Hardy arguably uses the same rhyme scheme throughout to reflect the inevitability of death and grief as a result of war. The rhyme scheme becomes a pattern in the same way that death and devastation becomes a pattern in war.

9859.belief: The dying soldier was already dead when he was thrown into the wagon.
9859.statement: Students often think that the dying soldier was already dead when he was thrown into the wagon.
9859.correction: It is important that students understand that the soldier was still half-alive when he was tossed, dying, into the body wagon. This needs to be understood for students to grasp the brutality of war and the lack of respect soldiers were shown.

9734.statement: Students sometimes fail to recognise that the tense shifts as the poem progresses.
9734.correction: Owen includes three tenses in his poem, perhaps to illustrate that the impact of war has, is and will be felt in his past, present and future.

9830.belief: That, because society was very religious in the 18th century, that Blake must have been a devout Christian too.
9830.statement: Students often think that, because society was very religious in the 18th century, that Blake must have been a devout Christian too.
9830.correction: Blake was extremely opposed to mass worship and hated the fact that religion was allied with the Government - he felt this gave institutions the ability to control and oppress people.

9008.belief: The Romantics were known for writing about love and romance.
9008.statement: The Romantics were known for writing about love and romance.
9008.correction: The Romantics are not to be confused with 'romantics' who may write love poetry. The Romantics most commonly wrote about nature and were known for critiquing the direction of society's progress.

9853.belief: Dharker is critical of the structures in the slums.
9853.statement: Students think that Dharker is critical of the structures in the slums.
9853.correction: Though Dharker portrays how dangerous these buildings are, she also shows great admiration of the slum community's resourcefulness in building theses structures - she celebrates their fortitude and resilience in the face of adversity.

9877.belief: Hughes wrote this poem about fascist dictators like Hitler.
9877.statement: Students think that Hughes wrote this poem about fascist dictators like Hitler.
9877.correction: Hughes stated that this was not his intention. Though the poem can be interpreted in this way, this was not what Hughes set out to convey - he wanted to convey the power of nature.

9791.statement: Students recognise that the hawk is powerful and don't explore this any further.
9791.correction: The significant question in the poem is arguably what makes the hawk powerful? Is it nature? Instinct? His physical strength? His intelligence?

9944.belief: This sonnet was written whilst Barrett Browning was married.
9944.statement: Students might think that this sonnet was written whilst Barrett Browning was married.
9944.correction: This poem was written before the pair were married. Barrett Browning knew of her father's disapproval, but loved Robert Browning very much.

6430.statement: Pupils often fail to notice or appreciate how defiant this poem is at the end.
6430.correction: In saying that she will love her future husband "better" after death, Barrett Browning defies her father and any cosmic force which may try to prevent the couple from being together. Barrett Browning's passion and commitment to Browning is evident.

9919.belief: This poem was written from one lover to another.
9919.statement: Students might think that this poem was written from one lover to another.
9919.correction: This poem is about Lord Byron's first encounter with his cousin's wife - as far as we know, he doesn't interact with her or pursue her - he merely observes her beauty from afar.
